/-
Author: @toskua
-/
module

public import MathlibExt.Analysis.VonNeumannAlgebra.PositiveOrderNormalMembership
public import MathlibExt.Analysis.VonNeumannAlgebra.Weight.GNSCoefficientOrderNormal

/-!
# The actual GNS diagonal coefficient of a normal weight is a normal functional

Normality of the original scalar weight makes its existing positive GNS
diagonal coefficient preserve original bounded positive-family LUBs. The
strict membership criterion applies to that same bounded map and gives a
member of the existing canonical normal-functional space. No normal member,
GNS model, family, limit or norm certificate is supplied as an input.
Faithfulness, semifiniteness and representation normality remain separate.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

open CStarAlgebra.ScalarWeight

namespace VonNeumannAlgebra

noncomputable section

universe u

variable {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H]

/-- Construct the actual normal-functional member of the original normal-weight GNS diagonal coefficient. -/
def normalWeightGNSDiagonalFunctional (M : VonNeumannAlgebra H) (φ : Weight M)
    (hφ : IsNormalWeight M φ) (x : φ.finiteSquareSubmodule) : normalFunctionalSpace M := by
  let : PartialOrder M := CStarAlgebra.spectralOrder M
  let : PartialOrder ℂ := CStarAlgebra.spectralOrder ℂ
  let ψ := φ.gnsDiagonalPositiveFunctional x
  have hmember : ψ.toContinuousLinearMap ∈ normalFunctionalSpace M := by
    apply positiveFunctional_mem_normalFunctionalSpace_of_positiveLUBs M ψ
    intro I _preorder _directed _nonempty a s hmono hbound hLUB
    exact gnsDiagonalPositiveFunctional_preserves_boundedPositiveIsLUB M φ hφ x a s
      hmono hbound hLUB
  exact ⟨ψ.toContinuousLinearMap, hmember⟩

/-- Coercion of the actual normal diagonal member is the same original GNS representation coefficient. -/
@[simp]
theorem normalWeightGNSDiagonalFunctional_coe (M : VonNeumannAlgebra H) (φ : Weight M)
    (hφ : IsNormalWeight M φ) (x : φ.finiteSquareSubmodule) :
    (normalWeightGNSDiagonalFunctional M φ hφ x : StrongDual ℂ M) =
      MathlibExt.Analysis.CStarAlgebra.representationCoefficient
        φ.gnsLeftStarAlgHom (φ.gnsMap x) (φ.gnsMap x) :=
  rfl

/-- The actual normal diagonal member has its original completed GNS vector value. -/
theorem normalWeightGNSDiagonalFunctional_apply (M : VonNeumannAlgebra H) (φ : Weight M)
    (hφ : IsNormalWeight M φ) (x : φ.finiteSquareSubmodule) (a : M) :
    (normalWeightGNSDiagonalFunctional M φ hφ x : StrongDual ℂ M) a =
      inner ℂ (φ.gnsMap x) ((φ.gnsLeftStarAlgHom a) (φ.gnsMap x)) := by
  rw [normalWeightGNSDiagonalFunctional_coe,
    MathlibExt.Analysis.CStarAlgebra.representationCoefficient_apply]

end

end VonNeumannAlgebra

/-
Author: @toskua
-/
module

public import MathlibExt.Analysis.VonNeumannAlgebra.Weight.GNSNormalCoefficients
public import MathlibExt.Analysis.VonNeumannAlgebra.NormalHom.VectorFunctionalCriterion

/-!
# The original normal weight has its computed normal GNS star homomorphism

The existing original unital GNS star map is restricted to the full concrete
operator von Neumann algebra on its actual Hilbert completion. Every vector
functional pullback is exactly its original GNS representation coefficient,
whose actual normal membership is proved from the original normal weight.
The stock vector-functional criterion constructs normality of that same
map. No normal homomorphism, GNS model or output certificate is supplied.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

open CStarAlgebra.ScalarWeight
open MathlibExt.Analysis.CStarAlgebra
open scoped CStarAlgebra

namespace VonNeumannAlgebra

noncomputable section

universe u

variable {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H]

/-- Construct normality of the same original completed weight GNS star representation. -/
def normalWeightGNSStarAlgHom (M : VonNeumannAlgebra H) (φ : Weight M)
    (hφ : IsNormalWeight M φ) : NormalStarAlgHom M (⊤ : VonNeumannAlgebra φ.GNS) := by
  let N : VonNeumannAlgebra φ.GNS := ⊤
  let f : M →⋆ₐ[ℂ] N := φ.gnsLeftStarAlgHom.codRestrict N.toStarSubalgebra (by
    intro a
    change φ.gnsLeftStarAlgHom a ∈ (⊤ : StarSubalgebra ℂ (φ.GNS →L[ℂ] φ.GNS))
    exact Set.mem_univ _)
  refine NormalStarAlgHom.ofVectorFunctionalPullbacks f ?_
  intro ξ η
  have hvalue : (vectorFunctional N ξ η).comp
      (⟨LinearMap.ofClass f, map_continuous f⟩ : M →L[ℂ] N) =
      representationCoefficient φ.gnsLeftStarAlgHom η ξ := by
    apply ContinuousLinearMap.ext
    intro a
    change vectorFunctional N ξ η (f a) = representationCoefficient φ.gnsLeftStarAlgHom η ξ a
    rw [vectorFunctional_apply, representationCoefficient_apply]
    rfl
  rw [hvalue]
  exact normalWeightGNSCoefficient_mem M φ hφ η ξ

/-- The actual normal map keeps the same original completed GNS operator at every source element. -/
@[simp]
theorem normalWeightGNSStarAlgHom_apply (M : VonNeumannAlgebra H) (φ : Weight M)
    (hφ : IsNormalWeight M φ) (a : M) :
    (normalWeightGNSStarAlgHom M φ hφ a : φ.GNS →L[ℂ] φ.GNS) = φ.gnsLeftStarAlgHom a :=
  rfl

end

end VonNeumannAlgebra

/-
Author: @toskua
-/
module

public import MathlibExt.Analysis.VonNeumannAlgebra.Weight.GNSNormalDiagonalFunctional
public import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.LinearMap

/-!
# Original normal-weight GNS off-diagonal coefficients in the actual normal span

Four actual normal diagonal members at x+y, x-y, x+i*y and x-i*y combine
by the original complex polarization identity. Their literal GNS map values
and second-variable-linear pairing give the off-diagonal representation
coefficient on the same original algebra. No desired normality, vector,
GNS model or coefficient-bound certificate is an input.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

open CStarAlgebra.ScalarWeight
open scoped InnerProductSpace

namespace VonNeumannAlgebra

noncomputable section

universe u

variable {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H]

/-- Construct the original off-diagonal GNS coefficient as an actual normal-functional member. -/
def normalWeightGNSOffDiagonalFunctional (M : VonNeumannAlgebra H) (φ : Weight M)
    (hφ : IsNormalWeight M φ) (x y : φ.finiteSquareSubmodule) :
    {ρ : normalFunctionalSpace M // (ρ.val : StrongDual ℂ M) =
      MathlibExt.Analysis.CStarAlgebra.representationCoefficient φ.gnsLeftStarAlgHom (φ.gnsMap x) (φ.gnsMap y)} := by
  let D := normalWeightGNSDiagonalFunctional M φ hφ
  let ρ : normalFunctionalSpace M := (4 : ℂ)⁻¹ •
    (D (x + y) - D (x - y) + Complex.I • D (x + Complex.I • y) -
      Complex.I • D (x - Complex.I • y))
  refine ⟨ρ, ?_⟩
  apply ContinuousLinearMap.ext
  intro a
  have hD (z : φ.finiteSquareSubmodule) :
      (D z : StrongDual ℂ M) a = ⟪φ.gnsMap z, (φ.gnsLeftStarAlgHom a) (φ.gnsMap z)⟫_ℂ := by
    exact normalWeightGNSDiagonalFunctional_apply M φ hφ z a
  change (4 : ℂ)⁻¹ • ((D (x + y) : StrongDual ℂ M) a - (D (x - y) : StrongDual ℂ M) a +
    Complex.I • (D (x + Complex.I • y) : StrongDual ℂ M) a -
    Complex.I • (D (x - Complex.I • y) : StrongDual ℂ M) a) = _
  rw [hD, hD, hD, hD, MathlibExt.Analysis.CStarAlgebra.representationCoefficient_apply]
  simp only [map_add, map_sub, map_smul, inner_add_left, inner_add_right,
    inner_sub_left, inner_sub_right, inner_smul_left, inner_smul_right,
    Complex.conj_I, smul_eq_mul]
  ring_nf
  rw [Complex.I_sq]
  ring

end

end VonNeumannAlgebra

/-
  Author: @toskua
-/
module

public import Mathlib.FieldTheory.Galois.Basic
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Dual.Lemmas
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.Free
public import Mathlib.RingTheory.TensorProduct.Maps
public import Mathlib.RingTheory.TensorProduct.Pi

/-!
# Canonical finite-Galois self-tensor decomposition

For a finite Galois extension `L/F`, the canonical original tensor map
`x ⊗ y ↦ (σ ↦ x * σ(y))` is an `L`-algebra equivalence.
The generic construction and its proofs retain their existing public names.
-/

@[expose] public section

noncomputable section

set_option autoImplicit false

open scoped TensorProduct

universe u

namespace MilnorK

variable (F L : Type u) [Field F] [Field L] [Algebra F L]

/-- Canonical tensor coordinates: `x ⊗ y` has `σ`-coordinate
`x * σ(y)`.  The tensor product uses its left `L`-algebra structure. -/
noncomputable def finiteGaloisTensorToFunctions :
    letI := Algebra.TensorProduct.leftAlgebra
      (R := F) (S := L) (A := L) (B := L)
    L ⊗[F] L →ₐ[L] ((L ≃ₐ[F] L) → L) :=
  Algebra.TensorProduct.lift
    (AlgHom.pi (fun _ : L ≃ₐ[F] L => AlgHom.id L L))
    (AlgHom.pi (fun σ : L ≃ₐ[F] L => σ.toAlgHom))
    (fun _ _ => Commute.all _ _)

@[simp]
theorem finiteGaloisTensorToFunctions_tmul (x y : L) :
    finiteGaloisTensorToFunctions F L (x ⊗ₜ[F] y) =
      fun σ : L ≃ₐ[F] L => x * σ y := by
  funext σ
  rw [finiteGaloisTensorToFunctions, Algebra.TensorProduct.lift_tmul]
  rfl

/-- The `σ`-coordinate of the canonical self-tensor map, regarded as an
`L`-linear functional. -/
private noncomputable def tensorCoordinateLinear
    (σ : L ≃ₐ[F] L) : Module.Dual L (L ⊗[F] L) :=
  (LinearMap.proj σ).comp (finiteGaloisTensorToFunctions F L).toLinearMap

/-- Restrict an `L`-linear tensor functional to `1 ⊗ L`. -/
private noncomputable def tensorDualRestrictRight :
    Module.Dual L (L ⊗[F] L) →ₗ[L] (L →ₗ[F] L) :=
  (LinearMap.applyₗ (1 : L)).comp
    (TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.lcurry F L L L L L)

private theorem tensorDualRestrictRight_coordinate
    (σ : L ≃ₐ[F] L) :
    tensorDualRestrictRight F L (tensorCoordinateLinear F L σ) =
      σ.toAlgHom.toLinearMap := by
  ext y
  simp [tensorDualRestrictRight, tensorCoordinateLinear,
    finiteGaloisTensorToFunctions_tmul]

private theorem tensorCoordinateLinear_linearIndependent :
    LinearIndependent L (tensorCoordinateLinear F L) := by
  apply LinearIndependent.of_comp (tensorDualRestrictRight F L)
  simpa [Function.comp_def, tensorDualRestrictRight_coordinate] using
    ((linearIndependent_algHom_toLinearMap F L L).comp
      (fun σ : L ≃ₐ[F] L => σ.toAlgHom)
      AlgEquiv.coe_toAlgHom_injective)

variable [FiniteDimensional F L] [IsGalois F L]

/-- The canonical finite-Galois tensor-coordinate map is injective. -/
theorem finiteGaloisTensorToFunctions_injective :
    Function.Injective (finiteGaloisTensorToFunctions F L) := by
  have hspan : Submodule.span L
      (Set.range (tensorCoordinateLinear F L)) = ⊤ :=
    (tensorCoordinateLinear_linearIndependent F L).span_eq_top_of_card_eq_finrank
      (by
        rw [Subspace.dual_finrank_eq]
        simp only [Module.finrank_tensorProduct, Module.finrank_self, one_mul]
        exact (Nat.card_eq_fintype_card (α := L ≃ₐ[F] L)).symm.trans
          (IsGalois.card_aut_eq_finrank F L))
  apply (injective_iff_map_eq_zero (finiteGaloisTensorToFunctions F L)).mpr
  intro x hx
  apply (Module.forall_dual_apply_eq_zero_iff L x).mp
  intro φ
  have hmem : φ ∈ Submodule.span L
      (Set.range (tensorCoordinateLinear F L)) := by
    rw [hspan]
    exact Submodule.mem_top
  refine Submodule.span_induction
    (p := fun f : Module.Dual L (L ⊗[F] L) => fun _ => f x = 0)
    ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ hmem
  · rintro f ⟨σ, rfl⟩
    change finiteGaloisTensorToFunctions F L x σ = 0
    rw [hx]
    rfl
  · exact LinearMap.zero_apply _
  · intro f g _ _ hf hg
    change f x + g x = 0
    rw [hf, hg, add_zero]
  · intro c f _ hf
    simp [hf]

/-- The canonical finite-Galois tensor-coordinate map is surjective. -/
theorem finiteGaloisTensorToFunctions_surjective :
    Function.Surjective (finiteGaloisTensorToFunctions F L) := by
  apply (LinearMap.injective_iff_surjective_of_finrank_eq_finrank ?_).mp
    (finiteGaloisTensorToFunctions_injective F L)
  simp only [Module.finrank_tensorProduct, Module.finrank_self, one_mul,
    Module.finrank_fintype_fun_eq_card]
  exact (IsGalois.card_aut_eq_finrank F L).symm.trans
    (Nat.card_eq_fintype_card (α := L ≃ₐ[F] L))

/-- The canonical finite-Galois tensor-coordinate map is bijective. -/
theorem finiteGaloisTensorToFunctions_bijective :
    Function.Bijective (finiteGaloisTensorToFunctions F L) :=
  ⟨finiteGaloisTensorToFunctions_injective F L,
    finiteGaloisTensorToFunctions_surjective F L⟩

/-- The finite-Galois self-tensor decomposition as an `L`-algebra
equivalence. -/
noncomputable def finiteGaloisTensorProductEquiv :
    letI := Algebra.TensorProduct.leftAlgebra
      (R := F) (S := L) (A := L) (B := L)
    L ⊗[F] L ≃ₐ[L] ((L ≃ₐ[F] L) → L) :=
  AlgEquiv.ofBijective (finiteGaloisTensorToFunctions F L)
    (finiteGaloisTensorToFunctions_bijective F L)

@[simp]
theorem finiteGaloisTensorProductEquiv_apply (z : L ⊗[F] L) :
    finiteGaloisTensorProductEquiv F L z =
      finiteGaloisTensorToFunctions F L z :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem finiteGaloisTensorProductEquiv_tmul
    (x y : L) (σ : L ≃ₐ[F] L) :
    finiteGaloisTensorProductEquiv F L (x ⊗ₜ[F] y) σ =
      x * σ y :=
  congrFun (finiteGaloisTensorToFunctions_tmul F L x y) σ

end MilnorK

-- Author: @toskua, Avocado
module

public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Alternating.Basic

/-!
# Restriction of scalars for alternating maps

An alternating map over an algebra is also alternating over the base ring
when the source and target scalar actions form scalar towers.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u v w z

namespace AlternatingMap

variable {R : Type u} {S : Type v}
variable [CommSemiring R] [Semiring S] [Algebra R S]
variable {M : Type w} [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [Module S M]
  [IsScalarTower R S M]
variable {N : Type z} [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N] [Module S N]
  [IsScalarTower R S N]
variable {ι : Type*}

/-- Restrict the scalars of an alternating map along an algebra. -/
def restrictScalars (f : M [⋀^ι]→ₗ[S] N) : M [⋀^ι]→ₗ[R] N :=
  { f.toMultilinearMap.restrictScalars R with
    map_eq_zero_of_eq' := f.map_eq_zero_of_eq }

@[simp]
theorem coe_restrictScalars (f : M [⋀^ι]→ₗ[S] N) :
    ⇑(f.restrictScalars (R := R)) = f :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem restrictScalars_apply (f : M [⋀^ι]→ₗ[S] N) (a : ι → M) :
    f.restrictScalars (R := R) a = f a :=
  rfl

end AlternatingMap

-- Author: @toskua, Avocado
module

public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Dimension.Constructions

/-!
# Bases adapted to a finite filtration

This file assembles bases of the successive quotients of an increasing
filtration into a basis of a finite filtration stage.  It also records the
chosen representative of every graded basis vector in the stage where that
vector is introduced.

## Main declarations

* `Module.Basis.FiltrationIndex` is the dependent sum of the graded basis
  indices below a finite cutoff.
* `Module.Basis.ofFiltrationStage` is the resulting basis of a finite
  filtration stage.
* `Module.Basis.ofFiltrationStageVector` regards a basis vector as an element
  of the stage where it is introduced.
* `Module.Basis.ofFiltration` specializes the construction when the final
  stage is the whole ambient module.

## Informal proof

Let `F 0 <= F 1 <= ...` be a filtration with `F 0 = 0`, and suppose that the
quotient `F (i+1) / F i` has a basis indexed by `kappa i`.  We argue by
induction on the cutoff `n`.

For `n = 0`, the stage `F 0` is the zero module, so its empty family is a
basis.  For the induction step, identify `F n` with its image as a submodule
of `F (n+1)`.  Mathlib's `Module.Basis.sumQuot` combines the transported basis
of this submodule with arbitrary representatives of the supplied basis of
`F (n+1) / F n`.  Its index type is the disjoint sum of the old indices and
`kappa n`; reindexing by the evident equivalence identifies this sum with
`Sigma i : Fin (n+1), kappa i`.

The `sumQuot_inl` formula says that every old vector is carried forward
without changing its ambient value.  The `sumQuot_inr` formula says that each
new vector maps to the prescribed quotient-basis vector.  Induction therefore
shows that every final basis vector still lies in the stage where it was
introduced and has exactly the prescribed image in the corresponding
successive quotient.  If the final stage is the top submodule, its canonical
linear equivalence with the ambient module transports this stage basis to a
basis of the ambient module without changing any underlying vector.
-/

@[expose] public section

universe u v w

namespace Module.Basis

variable {R : Type u} {M : Type v} [CommRing R]
variable [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]

/-- The dependent sum of the graded basis indices strictly below `n`. -/
abbrev FiltrationIndex (κ : ℕ → Type w) (n : ℕ) :=
  Σ i : Fin n, κ i.val

/-- Add the last graded index to the dependent sum of the preceding indices. -/
def filtrationIndexSuccEquiv (κ : ℕ → Type w) (n : ℕ) :
    FiltrationIndex κ n ⊕ κ n ≃ FiltrationIndex κ (n + 1) where
  toFun
    | Sum.inl ⟨i, a⟩ => ⟨i.castSucc, a⟩
    | Sum.inr a => ⟨Fin.last n, a⟩
  invFun p :=
    Fin.lastCases (fun a => Sum.inr a)
      (fun i a => Sum.inl ⟨i, a⟩) p.1 p.2
  left_inv x := by
    rcases x with (⟨i, a⟩ | a)
    · simp
    · simp
  right_inv p := by
    rcases p with ⟨i, a⟩
    revert a
    refine Fin.lastCases ?_ (fun j => ?_) i
    · intro a
      simp
    · intro a
      simp

@[simp]
theorem filtrationIndexSuccEquiv_apply_inl
    (κ : ℕ → Type w) (n : ℕ) (i : Fin n) (a : κ i.val) :
    filtrationIndexSuccEquiv κ n (Sum.inl ⟨i, a⟩) = ⟨i.castSucc, a⟩ :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem filtrationIndexSuccEquiv_apply_inr
    (κ : ℕ → Type w) (n : ℕ) (a : κ n) :
    filtrationIndexSuccEquiv κ n (Sum.inr a) = ⟨Fin.last n, a⟩ :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem filtrationIndexSuccEquiv_symm_castSucc
    (κ : ℕ → Type w) (n : ℕ) (i : Fin n) (a : κ i.val) :
    (filtrationIndexSuccEquiv κ n).symm ⟨i.castSucc, a⟩ =
      Sum.inl ⟨i, a⟩ := by
  simp [filtrationIndexSuccEquiv]

@[simp]
theorem filtrationIndexSuccEquiv_symm_last
    (κ : ℕ → Type w) (n : ℕ) (a : κ n) :
    (filtrationIndexSuccEquiv κ n).symm ⟨Fin.last n, a⟩ =
      Sum.inr a := by
  simp [filtrationIndexSuccEquiv]

/-- A basis of a finite filtration stage assembled from bases of all its
successive quotients.

The filtration is indexed by natural numbers, while `n` selects the finite
segment used by this construction.  The result is indexed by the dependent
sum of the supplied graded basis indices. -/
noncomputable def ofFiltrationStage
    (F : ℕ → Submodule R M) (hzero : F 0 = ⊥) (κ : ℕ → Type w) :
    ∀ n,
      (∀ i : Fin n, F i.val ≤ F (i.val + 1)) →
      (∀ i : Fin n,
        Basis (κ i.val) R
          (F (i.val + 1) ⧸ (F i.val).comap (F (i.val + 1)).subtype)) →
      Basis (FiltrationIndex κ n) R (F n)
  | 0, _, _ => by
      letI : Subsingleton (F 0) := by
        rw [hzero]
        infer_instance
      exact Basis.empty (F 0)
  | n + 1, hF, b =>
      let hF' : ∀ i : Fin n, F i.val ≤ F (i.val + 1) :=
        fun i => hF i.castSucc
      let b' : ∀ i : Fin n,
          Basis (κ i.val) R
            (F (i.val + 1) ⧸ (F i.val).comap (F (i.val + 1)).subtype) :=
        fun i => b i.castSucc
      let hlast : F n ≤ F (n + 1) := by
        simpa using hF (Fin.last n)
      let blast : Basis (κ n) R
          (F (n + 1) ⧸ (F n).comap (F (n + 1)).subtype) := by
        simpa using b (Fin.last n)
      let lower : Basis (FiltrationIndex κ n) R
          ((F n).comap (F (n + 1)).subtype) :=
        (ofFiltrationStage F hzero κ n hF' b').map
          (Submodule.comapSubtypeEquivOfLe hlast).symm
      (lower.sumQuot blast).reindex (filtrationIndexSuccEquiv κ n)

/-- Passing to the next filtration stage does not change an earlier basis
vector as an element of the ambient module. -/
@[simp]
theorem ofFiltrationStage_castSucc
    (F : ℕ → Submodule R M) (hzero : F 0 = ⊥) (κ : ℕ → Type w)
    (n : ℕ) (hF : ∀ j : Fin (n + 1), F j.val ≤ F (j.val + 1))
    (b : ∀ j : Fin (n + 1),
      Basis (κ j.val) R
        (F (j.val + 1) ⧸ (F j.val).comap (F (j.val + 1)).subtype))
    (i : Fin n) (a : κ i.val) :
    ((ofFiltrationStage F hzero κ (n + 1) hF b
        ⟨i.castSucc, a⟩ : F (n + 1)) : M) =
      (ofFiltrationStage F hzero κ n (fun j => hF j.castSucc)
        (fun j => b j.castSucc) ⟨i, a⟩ : F n) := by
  simp [ofFiltrationStage]

/-- The vector added at the last step maps to the prescribed basis vector of
the last successive quotient. -/
@[simp]
theorem ofFiltrationStage_last_mk
    (F : ℕ → Submodule R M) (hzero : F 0 = ⊥) (κ : ℕ → Type w)
    (n : ℕ)
    (hF : ∀ i : Fin (n + 1), F i.val ≤ F (i.val + 1))
    (b : ∀ i : Fin (n + 1),
      Basis (κ i.val) R
        (F (i.val + 1) ⧸ (F i.val).comap (F (i.val + 1)).subtype))
    (a : κ n) :
    Submodule.Quotient.mk
        (ofFiltrationStage F hzero κ (n + 1) hF b ⟨Fin.last n, a⟩) =
      b (Fin.last n) a := by
  simp [ofFiltrationStage]

/-- Every assembled basis vector belongs to the filtration stage where its
graded index is introduced. -/
theorem ofFiltrationStage_mem
    (F : ℕ → Submodule R M) (hzero : F 0 = ⊥) (κ : ℕ → Type w)
    (n : ℕ) (hF : ∀ j : Fin n, F j.val ≤ F (j.val + 1))
    (b : ∀ j : Fin n,
      Basis (κ j.val) R
        (F (j.val + 1) ⧸ (F j.val).comap (F (j.val + 1)).subtype))
    (i : Fin n) (a : κ i.val) :
    ((ofFiltrationStage F hzero κ n hF b ⟨i, a⟩ : F n) : M) ∈
      F (i.val + 1) := by
  induction n with
  | zero => exact Fin.elim0 i
  | succ n ih =>
      revert a
      refine Fin.lastCases ?_ (fun j => ?_) i
      · intro a
        exact (ofFiltrationStage F hzero κ (n + 1) hF b
          ⟨Fin.last n, a⟩).property
      · intro a
        rw [ofFiltrationStage_castSucc]
        exact ih (fun k => hF k.castSucc) (fun k => b k.castSucc) j a

/-- An assembled basis vector, restricted to the filtration stage where it
is introduced. -/
noncomputable def ofFiltrationStageVector
    (F : ℕ → Submodule R M) (hzero : F 0 = ⊥) (κ : ℕ → Type w)
    (n : ℕ)
    (hF : ∀ i : Fin n, F i.val ≤ F (i.val + 1))
    (b : ∀ i : Fin n,
      Basis (κ i.val) R
        (F (i.val + 1) ⧸ (F i.val).comap (F (i.val + 1)).subtype))
    (i : Fin n) (a : κ i.val) : F (i.val + 1) :=
  ⟨ofFiltrationStage F hzero κ n hF b ⟨i, a⟩,
    ofFiltrationStage_mem F hzero κ n hF b i a⟩

/-- Every assembled filtration vector is an exact representative of the
supplied basis vector in its successive quotient. -/
@[simp]
theorem ofFiltrationStageVector_mk
    (F : ℕ → Submodule R M) (hzero : F 0 = ⊥) (κ : ℕ → Type w)
    (n : ℕ)
    (hF : ∀ i : Fin n, F i.val ≤ F (i.val + 1))
    (b : ∀ i : Fin n,
      Basis (κ i.val) R
        (F (i.val + 1) ⧸ (F i.val).comap (F (i.val + 1)).subtype))
    (i : Fin n) (a : κ i.val) :
    Submodule.Quotient.mk
        (ofFiltrationStageVector F hzero κ n hF b i a) = b i a := by
  induction n with
  | zero => exact Fin.elim0 i
  | succ n ih =>
      revert a
      refine Fin.lastCases ?_ (fun j => ?_) i
      · intro a
        simp [ofFiltrationStageVector]
      · intro a
        simpa [ofFiltrationStageVector] using
          ih (fun k => hF k.castSucc) (fun k => b k.castSucc) j a

/-- A basis of the ambient module assembled from bases of the successive
quotients of a finite filtration from zero to the top submodule. -/
noncomputable def ofFiltration
    (F : ℕ → Submodule R M) (hzero : F 0 = ⊥) (κ : ℕ → Type w)
    (n : ℕ)
    (hF : ∀ i : Fin n, F i.val ≤ F (i.val + 1))
    (b : ∀ i : Fin n,
      Basis (κ i.val) R
        (F (i.val + 1) ⧸ (F i.val).comap (F (i.val + 1)).subtype))
    (htop : F n = ⊤) : Basis (FiltrationIndex κ n) R M :=
  (ofFiltrationStage F hzero κ n hF b).map
    ((LinearEquiv.ofEq (F n) ⊤ htop).trans Submodule.topEquiv)

/-- Mapping the final filtration stage to the ambient module does not change
the underlying basis vectors. -/
@[simp]
theorem ofFiltration_apply
    (F : ℕ → Submodule R M) (hzero : F 0 = ⊥) (κ : ℕ → Type w)
    (n : ℕ)
    (hF : ∀ i : Fin n, F i.val ≤ F (i.val + 1))
    (b : ∀ i : Fin n,
      Basis (κ i.val) R
        (F (i.val + 1) ⧸ (F i.val).comap (F (i.val + 1)).subtype))
    (htop : F n = ⊤) (p : FiltrationIndex κ n) :
    ofFiltration F hzero κ n hF b htop p =
      (ofFiltrationStage F hzero κ n hF b p : F n) := by
  simp [ofFiltration]

end Module.Basis

/-!
# Clearing a finite module into the lattice of a field basis

A single nonzero denominator carries the image of a finite module into
the full span over the original domain of a finite fraction-field basis.
The denominator is derived from the actual generator coordinates.
-/

@[expose] public section
noncomputable section

universe u v w z t

namespace Module.Basis

variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R]
variable {K : Type v} [Field K] [Algebra R K] [IsFractionRing R K]
variable {V : Type w} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [Module R V] [IsScalarTower R K V]
variable {M : Type z} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]

/-- The actual coordinates of a finite generating family earn a common
nonzero scalar carrying its entire image into the original domain span of
a finite fraction-field basis. Neither freeness of the source module nor
normality of the domain is needed. -/
theorem exists_scalar_image_mem_span {ι : Type t} [Finite ι]
    (b : Basis ι K V) (f : M →ₗ[R] V) :
    ∃ a : R, a ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ x : M, a • f x ∈ Submodule.span R (Set.range b) := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨n, s, hs⟩ := Module.Finite.exists_fin (R := R) (M := M)
  obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := IsLocalization.exist_integer_multiples_of_finite
    (nonZeroDivisors R) (fun p : Fin n × ι => b.repr (f (s p.1)) p.2)
  refine ⟨a, mem_nonZeroDivisors_iff_ne_zero.mp a.property, ?_⟩
  let q : Submodule R M := (Submodule.span R (Set.range b)).comap (a.val • f)
  have hgen : ∀ i : Fin n, s i ∈ q := by
    intro i
    change a.val • f (s i) ∈ Submodule.span R (Set.range b)
    apply (b.mem_span_iff_repr_mem R _).mpr
    intro j
    have h := ha (i, j)
    change b.repr.toLinearMap (a.val • f (s i)) j ∈ Set.range (algebraMap R K)
    rw [b.repr.toLinearMap.map_smul_of_tower]
    exact h
  have hq : ⊤ ≤ q := by
    rw [← hs]
    apply Submodule.span_le.mpr
    rintro x ⟨i, rfl⟩
    exact hgen i
  intro x
  exact hq (show x ∈ (⊤ : Submodule R M) from trivial)

end Module.Basis

public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.Basic

/-!
# Integer bilinear composition of tensor homomorphisms

The actual additive tensor map followed by an additive coefficient map
has its canonical curried integer-linear form. All group universes remain
independent.
-/

@[expose] public section
noncomputable section
set_option autoImplicit false
universe u v w z
open scoped TensorProduct

namespace AddMonoidHom
variable {A : Type u} {B : Type v} {C : Type w} {D : Type z}
variable [AddCommGroup A] [AddCommGroup B] [AddCommGroup C] [AddCommGroup D]
variable [Module ℤ A] [Module ℤ B] [Module ℤ D]

/-- A map additive in both arguments is integer bilinear for the
supplied integer module structures, by the actual integer scalar law. -/
def toIntBilinear (h : A →+ B →+ D) :
    A →ₗ[ℤ] B →ₗ[ℤ] D := by
  let k : A →+ (B →ₗ[ℤ] D) :=
    { toFun := fun x =>
        { toFun := h x
          map_add' := (h x).map_add
          map_smul' := fun r y => by
            simpa only [Int.cast_id, RingHom.id_apply] using map_intCast_smul (h x) ℤ ℤ r y }
      map_zero' := by
        ext y
        exact congrArg (fun a : B →+ D => a y) h.map_zero
      map_add' := by
        intro x z
        ext y
        exact congrArg (fun a : B →+ D => a y) (h.map_add x z) }
  exact
    { toFun := k
      map_add' := k.map_add
      map_smul' := fun r x => by
        simpa only [Int.cast_id, RingHom.id_apply] using map_intCast_smul k ℤ ℤ r x }

/-- Integer bilinear conversion evaluates the original additive map. -/
theorem toIntBilinear_apply (h : A →+ B →+ D) (x : A) (y : B) :
    toIntBilinear h x y = h x y := rfl

/-- Construct the same integer bilinear function directly from its
two additive laws, retaining arbitrary integer module structures. -/
def intBilinearOfAdd (f : A → B → D)
    (hLeft : ∀ x z y, f (x + z) y = f x y + f z y)
    (hRight : ∀ x y z, f x (y + z) = f x y + f x z) :
    A →ₗ[ℤ] B →ₗ[ℤ] D :=
  toIntBilinear <|
    AddMonoidHom.mk' (fun x => AddMonoidHom.mk' (f x) (hRight x))
      (fun x z => AddMonoidHom.ext fun y => hLeft x z y)

/-- Constructing integer bilinearity preserves the supplied function. -/
theorem intBilinearOfAdd_apply (f : A → B → D)
    (hLeft : ∀ x z y, f (x + z) y = f x y + f z y)
    (hRight : ∀ x y z, f x (y + z) = f x y + f x z) (x : A) (y : B) :
    intBilinearOfAdd f hLeft hRight x y = f x y := rfl

/-- Compose actual additive tensor and coefficient maps, then curry the
same function over the supplied integer module structures. -/
def compIntTensorBilinear (f : C →+ D) (g : A ⊗[ℤ] B →+ C) :
    A →ₗ[ℤ] B →ₗ[ℤ] D := by
  let h : A →+ B →+ D :=
    { toFun := fun x =>
        { toFun := fun y => f (g (x ⊗ₜ[ℤ] y))
          map_zero' := by simp only [TensorProduct.tmul_zero, map_zero]
          map_add' := by intro y z; simp only [TensorProduct.tmul_add, map_add] }
      map_zero' := by
        ext y
        change f (g ((0 : A) ⊗ₜ[ℤ] y)) = 0
        simp only [TensorProduct.zero_tmul, map_zero]
      map_add' := by
        intro x z
        ext y
        change f (g ((x + z) ⊗ₜ[ℤ] y)) = f (g (x ⊗ₜ[ℤ] y)) + f (g (z ⊗ₜ[ℤ] y))
        simp only [TensorProduct.add_tmul, map_add] }
  exact toIntBilinear h

/-- The curried bilinear map evaluates the original two additive maps
on the literal integer pure tensor. -/
theorem compIntTensorBilinear_apply (f : C →+ D) (g : A ⊗[ℤ] B →+ C) (x : A) (y : B) :
    compIntTensorBilinear f g x y = f (g (x ⊗ₜ[ℤ] y)) := rfl

end AddMonoidHom

module

public import Mathlib.Algebra.Algebra.Pi
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Charpoly.ToMatrix
import MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.Charpoly.FiniteFiltration

/-!
# Characteristic polynomials of dependent componentwise endomorphisms

Mathlib's `LinearMap.charpoly_prodMap` computes the characteristic
polynomial of a binary product endomorphism.  This file proves the
dependent-family version over a finite index type: the modules `M i` may
have different ranks, and the characteristic polynomial of the
componentwise endomorphism of `∀ i, M i` is the product of the component
characteristic polynomials.  It is the characteristic-polynomial analogue
of `LinearMap.det_pi_dependent` in
`MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.Determinant.DependentPi`.

## Main results

* `LinearMap.charpoly_pi_dependent`: the characteristic polynomial of a
  componentwise endomorphism of a finite dependent product is the product
  of the component characteristic polynomials.
* `Algebra.lmul_charpoly_eq_of_algEquiv`: the characteristic polynomial of
  left multiplication is invariant under algebra equivalence, paralleling
  `Algebra.norm_eq_of_algEquiv`.
* `Algebra.lmul_charpoly_pi_apply`: the characteristic polynomial of left
  multiplication by an element of a finite dependent product of algebras
  is the product of the component characteristic polynomials.

## Informal proof

The proof follows the pattern of `Algebra.norm_pi_apply` in
`MathlibExt.RingTheory.Norm.FiniteProduct`, rather than the block-diagonal
matrix computation used for determinants: `Matrix.charpoly`, unlike
`Matrix.det`, takes `DecidableEq` and `Fintype` instance arguments, and
the block-triangular route produces diagonal-block characteristic
polynomials whose fiber instances mix two different `DecidableEq`
sources, which do not unify with synthesized instances.  The induction
route only ever uses the ambient module instances.

For a product indexed by `Fin n`, induct on `n`.  The empty product is a
zero module, so its characteristic polynomial is `1`.  At the successor
step, split a dependent function into its zeroth coordinate and its tail.
Conjugating the componentwise endomorphism by this linear equivalence
gives the binary product of the head endomorphism and the componentwise
tail endomorphism; `LinearMap.charpoly_prodMap`, conjugation invariance,
and the induction hypothesis give the result.  Finally, reindex an
arbitrary finite type by `Fin (Fintype.card ι)`; conjugation invariance
of the characteristic polynomial and invariance of a finite product under
reindexing finish the proof.  Left multiplication on a product algebra
is componentwise by definition, and an algebra equivalence conjugates
left multiplication by `x` to left multiplication by its image, giving
the two algebra corollaries.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
noncomputable section

open scoped BigOperators
open Polynomial

universe uR uI uM uK

namespace LinearMap

variable {R : Type uR} [CommRing R]

/-- Split a dependent product over `Fin (n + 1)` into its head and tail
factors, as a linear equivalence. -/
private def piFinSuccLinearEquiv {n : ℕ} (M : Fin (n + 1) → Type uM)
    [∀ i, AddCommGroup (M i)] [∀ i, Module R (M i)] :
    (∀ i, M i) ≃ₗ[R] M 0 × (∀ i : Fin n, M (Fin.succ i)) where
  toFun f := (f 0, Fin.tail f)
  invFun p := Fin.cons p.1 p.2
  left_inv f := Fin.cons_self_tail f
  right_inv p := by
    ext
    · exact Fin.cons_zero p.1 p.2
    · exact Fin.cons_succ p.1 p.2 _
  map_add' _ _ := rfl
  map_smul' _ _ := rfl

/-- Conjugating a componentwise endomorphism over `Fin (n + 1)` by the
head-tail equivalence gives the binary product of the head endomorphism
and the componentwise tail endomorphism. -/
private theorem piFinSuccLinearEquiv_conj_pi {n : ℕ}
    {M : Fin (n + 1) → Type uM} [∀ i, AddCommGroup (M i)]
    [∀ i, Module R (M i)] (f : ∀ i, M i →ₗ[R] M i) :
    (piFinSuccLinearEquiv (R := R) M).conj
        (LinearMap.pi (fun i => (f i).comp (LinearMap.proj i))) =
      (f 0).prodMap
        (LinearMap.pi (fun i : Fin n => (f i.succ).comp
          (LinearMap.proj i))) := by
  apply LinearMap.ext
  rintro ⟨x, y⟩
  apply Prod.ext
  · rfl
  · funext i
    rfl

/-- The characteristic polynomial of a componentwise endomorphism of a
`Fin n`-indexed dependent product is the product of the component
characteristic polynomials. -/
private theorem charpoly_pi_dependent_fin {n : ℕ} {M : Fin n → Type uM}
    [∀ i, AddCommGroup (M i)] [∀ i, Module R (M i)]
    [∀ i, Module.Free R (M i)] [∀ i, Module.Finite R (M i)]
    (f : ∀ i, M i →ₗ[R] M i) :
    (LinearMap.pi (fun i => (f i).comp (LinearMap.proj i))).charpoly =
      ∏ i, (f i).charpoly := by
  induction n with
  | zero =>
    have : Subsingleton (∀ i, M i) :=
      ⟨fun _ _ => funext fun i => i.elim0⟩
    rw [LinearMap.charpoly_eq_one_of_subsingleton]
    simp
  | succ n ih =>
    calc
      (LinearMap.pi (fun i => (f i).comp (LinearMap.proj i))).charpoly =
          ((piFinSuccLinearEquiv (R := R) M).conj
            (LinearMap.pi (fun i => (f i).comp
              (LinearMap.proj i)))).charpoly :=
        (LinearEquiv.charpoly_conj _ _).symm
      _ = (f 0).charpoly *
            (LinearMap.pi (fun i : Fin n => (f i.succ).comp
              (LinearMap.proj i))).charpoly := by
        rw [piFinSuccLinearEquiv_conj_pi, LinearMap.charpoly_prodMap]
      _ = (f 0).charpoly * ∏ i : Fin n, (f i.succ).charpoly := by
        rw [ih (fun i => f i.succ)]
      _ = ∏ i, (f i).charpoly := by
        rw [Fin.prod_univ_succ]

variable {ι : Type uI} [Fintype ι]
variable {M : ι → Type uM}
variable [∀ i, AddCommGroup (M i)] [∀ i, Module R (M i)]
variable [∀ i, Module.Free R (M i)] [∀ i, Module.Finite R (M i)]

/-- Characteristic polynomial of a componentwise endomorphism of a finite
dependent product. The component modules may have unequal ranks. -/
theorem charpoly_pi_dependent (f : ∀ i, M i →ₗ[R] M i) :
    (LinearMap.pi (fun i => (f i).comp (LinearMap.proj i))).charpoly =
      ∏ i, (f i).charpoly := by
  classical
  let e := Fintype.equivFin ι
  have hconj : (LinearEquiv.piCongrLeft' R M e).conj
        (LinearMap.pi (fun i => (f i).comp (LinearMap.proj i))) =
      LinearMap.pi (fun j => (f (e.symm j)).comp (LinearMap.proj j)) := by
    apply LinearMap.ext
    intro g
    obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := (LinearEquiv.piCongrLeft' R M e).surjective g
    funext j
    simp [e]
  calc
    (LinearMap.pi (fun i => (f i).comp (LinearMap.proj i))).charpoly =
        ((LinearEquiv.piCongrLeft' R M e).conj
          (LinearMap.pi (fun i => (f i).comp
            (LinearMap.proj i)))).charpoly :=
      (LinearEquiv.charpoly_conj _ _).symm
    _ = ∏ j, (f (e.symm j)).charpoly := by
      rw [hconj, charpoly_pi_dependent_fin]
    _ = ∏ i, (f i).charpoly :=
      Fintype.prod_equiv e.symm _ _ (fun _ => rfl)

end LinearMap

namespace Algebra

variable {R : Type uR} [CommRing R]
variable {S : Type uM} {T : Type uK} [Ring S] [Ring T]
variable [Algebra R S] [Algebra R T]
variable [Module.Free R S] [Module.Finite R S]
variable [Module.Free R T] [Module.Finite R T]

/-- The characteristic polynomial of left multiplication is invariant under
algebra equivalence: an algebra equivalence conjugates left multiplication
by `x` to left multiplication by the image of `x`.  This parallels
`Algebra.norm_eq_of_algEquiv`. -/
theorem lmul_charpoly_eq_of_algEquiv (e : S ≃ₐ[R] T) (x : S) :
    (Algebra.lmul R T (e x)).charpoly =
      (Algebra.lmul R S x).charpoly := by
  rw [← LinearEquiv.charpoly_conj e.toLinearEquiv (Algebra.lmul R S x)]
  congr 1
  ext y
  simp [Algebra.coe_lmul_eq_mul]

variable {ι : Type uI} [Fintype ι] {A : ι → Type uM}
variable [∀ i, Ring (A i)] [∀ i, Algebra R (A i)]
variable [∀ i, Module.Free R (A i)] [∀ i, Module.Finite R (A i)]

/-- The characteristic polynomial of left multiplication by an element of a
finite dependent product of algebras is the product of the characteristic
polynomials of left multiplication by its components. -/
theorem lmul_charpoly_pi_apply (q : ∀ i, A i) :
    (Algebra.lmul R (∀ i, A i) q).charpoly =
      ∏ i, (Algebra.lmul R (A i) (q i)).charpoly := by
  classical
  have hmul : Algebra.lmul R (∀ i, A i) q =
      LinearMap.pi (fun i => (Algebra.lmul R (A i) (q i)).comp
        (LinearMap.proj i)) := by
    apply LinearMap.ext
    intro y
    funext i
    rfl
  rw [hmul, LinearMap.charpoly_pi_dependent]

end Algebra

end

module

public import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Fin
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Charpoly.ToMatrix
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.Charpoly.Basic
public import MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.Determinant.FiniteFiltration

/-!
# Characteristic polynomials along finite invariant filtrations

This file is the characteristic-polynomial analogue of
`MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.Determinant.FiniteFiltration`.  It packages and
iterates the characteristic-polynomial factorization for an endomorphism
preserving a submodule, for finite filtrations whose stages and successive
quotients are finite free modules.

## Main declarations

* `LinearMap.charpoly_eq_one_of_subsingleton` computes the characteristic
  polynomial on a zero module.
* `LinearMap.charpoly_eq_charpoly_mul_charpoly` is the raw one-step
  factorization for an invariant submodule, the characteristic-polynomial
  analogue of Mathlib's `LinearMap.det_eq_det_mul_det`.
* `LinearMap.InvariantExtension.charpoly_eq_charpoly_mul_charpoly_quotientMap`
  is the one-step factorization packaged by an invariant extension.
* `LinearMap.charpoly_eq_charpoly_mul_prod_graded` iterates the factorization
  through a finite tower.
* `LinearMap.charpoly_eq_prod_graded_of_bottom_subsingleton` removes the
  bottom factor when the initial stage is zero.

## Informal proof

For one step, choose a basis of the invariant submodule `S` and a basis of
`W / S`, and combine them into a basis of `W` with `Module.Basis.sumQuot`.
Exactly as in Mathlib's proof of `LinearMap.det_eq_det_mul_det`, the matrix
of the endomorphism in this basis is block upper-triangular, with diagonal
blocks the matrices of the restriction and of the quotient map.  The matrix
characteristic polynomial of a block upper-triangular matrix is the product
of the characteristic polynomials of its diagonal blocks
(`Matrix.charpoly_fromBlocks_zero₂₁`), which gives the raw factorization.

The stored intertwining equality in an invariant extension says that the
restriction is conjugate to the lower-stage endomorphism, and characteristic
polynomials are invariant under conjugation, giving the packaged one-step
formula.  The finite-tower formula is then the same `Fin n` induction as in
the determinant file: if `p_{i+1} = p_i * q_i`, then
`p_n = p_0 * ∏ i, q_i`.  When the bottom stage is a zero module, its
characteristic polynomial is `1` (the empty matrix), leaving only the
product over the graded quotients.

The freeness of every successive quotient is explicit, as in the determinant
file: over an arbitrary commutative ring it does not follow merely from
freeness of the two adjacent stages.  The upper stage is also assumed free;
unlike `LinearMap.det`, the characteristic polynomial is only defined on
finite free modules.
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped BigOperators
open Polynomial

universe u v w

namespace LinearMap

variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
variable {V : Type v} {W : Type w}
variable [AddCommGroup V] [Module R V]
variable [AddCommGroup W] [Module R W]

/-- The characteristic polynomial of an endomorphism of a zero module is
`1`, paralleling `LinearMap.det_eq_one_of_subsingleton`. -/
theorem charpoly_eq_one_of_subsingleton {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M]
    [Module R M] [Module.Free R M] [Module.Finite R M] [Subsingleton M]
    (f : M →ₗ[R] M) : f.charpoly = 1 := by
  have b : Module.Basis (Fin 0) R M := Module.Basis.empty M
  rw [← LinearMap.charpoly_toMatrix f b]
  exact Matrix.charpoly_isEmpty

open Module.Basis in
/-- Characteristic-polynomial factorization for an endomorphism preserving
a submodule: the characteristic polynomial is the product of those of the
restriction and of the induced quotient map.  This is the
characteristic-polynomial analogue of `LinearMap.det_eq_det_mul_det`, with
the same block upper-triangular matrix proof. -/
theorem charpoly_eq_charpoly_mul_charpoly (e : W →ₗ[R] W) (S : Submodule R W)
    (he : S ≤ S.comap e) [Module.Free R W] [Module.Finite R W]
    [Module.Free R S] [Module.Finite R S] [Module.Free R (W ⧸ S)] :
    e.charpoly = (e.restrict he).charpoly * (S.mapQ S e he).charpoly := by
  let m := Module.Free.ChooseBasisIndex R S
  let bW : Module.Basis m R S := Module.Free.chooseBasis R S
  let n := Module.Free.ChooseBasisIndex R (W ⧸ S)
  let bQ : Module.Basis n R (W ⧸ S) := Module.Free.chooseBasis R (W ⧸ S)
  let b := sumQuot bW bQ
  let A : Matrix m m R := LinearMap.toMatrix bW bW (e.restrict he)
  let B : Matrix m n R := Matrix.of fun i l ↦
    ((sumQuot bW bQ).repr (e ((sumQuot bW bQ) (Sum.inr l)))) (Sum.inl i)
  let D : Matrix n n R := LinearMap.toMatrix bQ bQ (S.mapQ S e he)
  suffices LinearMap.toMatrix b b e = Matrix.fromBlocks A B 0 D by
    rw [← LinearMap.charpoly_toMatrix e b, this,
      ← LinearMap.charpoly_toMatrix _ bW, ← LinearMap.charpoly_toMatrix _ bQ,
      Matrix.charpoly_fromBlocks_zero₂₁]
  ext u v
  cases u with
  | inl i =>
    cases v with
    | inl k =>
      simp only [b, sumQuot_inl, Matrix.fromBlocks_apply₁₁, A,
        LinearMap.toMatrix_apply]
      apply sumQuot_repr_inl_of_mem
    | inr l => simp [b, LinearMap.toMatrix_apply, Matrix.fromBlocks_apply₁₂, B]
  | inr j =>
    cases v with
    | inl k =>
      suffices S.mkQ (e (bW k)) = 0 by simp [LinearMap.toMatrix_apply, b, this]
      rw [← LinearMap.mem_ker, Submodule.ker_mkQ]
      exact he (Submodule.coe_mem (bW k))
    | inr l =>
      simp only [LinearMap.toMatrix_apply, sumQuot_repr_inr,
        Matrix.fromBlocks_apply₂₂, b, D]
      rw [← sumQuot_inr bW bQ l, S.mapQ_apply]
      simp

namespace InvariantExtension

variable {f : V →ₗ[R] V} {g : W →ₗ[R] W}

/-- Characteristic-polynomial factorization for one invariant extension.

This is the reusable one-step block-triangular formula, the
characteristic-polynomial analogue of
`LinearMap.InvariantExtension.det_eq_det_mul_det_quotientMap`.  The upper
stage is assumed free because `LinearMap.charpoly`, unlike `LinearMap.det`,
is only defined on finite free modules. -/
theorem charpoly_eq_charpoly_mul_charpoly_quotientMap
    (E : InvariantExtension f g) [Module.Free R V] [Module.Finite R V]
    [Module.Free R W] [Module.Finite R W]
    [Module.Free R (W ⧸ E.submodule)] :
    g.charpoly = f.charpoly * E.quotientMap.charpoly := by
  let _ : Module.Free R E.submodule := Module.Free.of_equiv E.equiv
  let _ : Module.Finite R E.submodule := Module.Finite.equiv E.equiv
  calc
    g.charpoly = (g.restrict E.stable).charpoly * E.quotientMap.charpoly :=
      g.charpoly_eq_charpoly_mul_charpoly E.submodule E.stable
    _ = f.charpoly * E.quotientMap.charpoly := by
      rw [← E.conjugate_eq]
      congr 1
      simpa only [LinearEquiv.conj_apply, LinearMap.comp_assoc] using
        (LinearEquiv.charpoly_conj E.equiv f)

end InvariantExtension

private theorem charpoly_last_eq_first_mul_prod {n : ℕ}
    (d : Fin (n + 1) → R[X]) (q : Fin n → R[X])
    (h : ∀ i, d i.succ = d i.castSucc * q i) :
    d (Fin.last n) = d 0 * ∏ i, q i := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp
  | succ n ih =>
      have hprefix :
          d (Fin.castSucc (Fin.last n)) =
            d 0 * ∏ i : Fin n, q i.castSucc := by
        apply ih (d := fun i ↦ d i.castSucc) (q := fun i ↦ q i.castSucc)
        intro i
        simpa using h i.castSucc
      calc
        d (Fin.last (n + 1)) =
            d (Fin.castSucc (Fin.last n)) * q (Fin.last n) := by
          simpa using h (Fin.last n)
        _ = (d 0 * ∏ i : Fin n, q i.castSucc) * q (Fin.last n) := by
          rw [hprefix]
        _ = d 0 * ((∏ i : Fin n, q i.castSucc) * q (Fin.last n)) := by
          rw [mul_assoc]
        _ = d 0 * ∏ i, q i := by
          rw [Fin.prod_univ_castSucc]

section FiniteTower

variable {n : ℕ} {M : Fin (n + 1) → Type v}
variable [∀ i, AddCommGroup (M i)] [∀ i, Module R (M i)]
variable [∀ i, Module.Free R (M i)] [∀ i, Module.Finite R (M i)]

/-- The characteristic polynomial on the final stage of a finite invariant
filtration is the characteristic polynomial on the initial stage times the
product of the characteristic polynomials on all successive graded
quotients.  This is the characteristic-polynomial analogue of
`LinearMap.det_eq_det_mul_prod_graded`, with the same interface: each
`step i` identifies stage `i` with an invariant submodule of stage `i+1`. -/
theorem charpoly_eq_charpoly_mul_prod_graded
    (endomorphism : ∀ i, M i →ₗ[R] M i)
    (step : ∀ i : Fin n,
      InvariantExtension (endomorphism i.castSucc) (endomorphism i.succ))
    (quotientFree : ∀ i, Module.Free R (M i.succ ⧸ (step i).submodule)) :
    (endomorphism (Fin.last n)).charpoly =
      (endomorphism 0).charpoly * ∏ i, (step i).quotientMap.charpoly := by
  refine charpoly_last_eq_first_mul_prod
    (d := fun i ↦ (endomorphism i).charpoly)
    (q := fun i ↦ (step i).quotientMap.charpoly) ?_
  intro i
  let _ : Module.Free R (M i.succ ⧸ (step i).submodule) := quotientFree i
  exact (step i).charpoly_eq_charpoly_mul_charpoly_quotientMap

/-- Version of `LinearMap.charpoly_eq_charpoly_mul_prod_graded` for a
filtration whose bottom characteristic polynomial has already been
identified with one. -/
theorem charpoly_eq_prod_graded_of_bottom_charpoly_eq_one
    (endomorphism : ∀ i, M i →ₗ[R] M i)
    (step : ∀ i : Fin n,
      InvariantExtension (endomorphism i.castSucc) (endomorphism i.succ))
    (quotientFree : ∀ i, Module.Free R (M i.succ ⧸ (step i).submodule))
    (hbottom : (endomorphism 0).charpoly = 1) :
    (endomorphism (Fin.last n)).charpoly =
      ∏ i, (step i).quotientMap.charpoly := by
  rw [charpoly_eq_charpoly_mul_prod_graded endomorphism step quotientFree,
    hbottom, one_mul]

/-- Characteristic-polynomial product formula for a finite invariant
filtration starting at a zero module. -/
theorem charpoly_eq_prod_graded_of_bottom_subsingleton
    (endomorphism : ∀ i, M i →ₗ[R] M i)
    (step : ∀ i : Fin n,
      InvariantExtension (endomorphism i.castSucc) (endomorphism i.succ))
    (quotientFree : ∀ i, Module.Free R (M i.succ ⧸ (step i).submodule))
    [Subsingleton (M 0)] :
    (endomorphism (Fin.last n)).charpoly =
      ∏ i, (step i).quotientMap.charpoly :=
  charpoly_eq_prod_graded_of_bottom_charpoly_eq_one endomorphism step
    quotientFree (LinearMap.charpoly_eq_one_of_subsingleton _)

end FiniteTower

end LinearMap

-- Author: @toskua, Avocado
module

public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Charpoly.Basic

/-!
# Minimal and characteristic polynomials of left multiplication

If the natural degree of `minpoly K x` is the finrank of the
finite-dimensional algebra `E`, the characteristic polynomial of left
multiplication by `x` is the minimal polynomial. Both are monic, the
minimal polynomial divides the characteristic polynomial by the existing
Cayley--Hamilton evaluation theorem, and their natural degrees agree.

The underlying polynomial-evaluation, integrality and minimal-polynomial
transport facts are supplied by Mathlib's algebra-homomorphism APIs.
The algebra need not be commutative, reduced or a domain. Finite
dimensionality already supplies the integrality of `x`.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false

open Polynomial

namespace LinearMap

section Primitive

variable {K E : Type*} [Field K] [Ring E] [Algebra K E]
  [FiniteDimensional K E]

/-- If the minimal polynomial of `x` has natural degree equal to the
finrank of the algebra, it is the characteristic polynomial of left
multiplication by `x`. Finite dimensionality supplies integrality. -/
theorem charpoly_lmul_eq_minpoly_of_natDegree_eq_finrank
    (x : E) (hDeg : (minpoly K x).natDegree = Module.finrank K E) :
    (Algebra.lmul K E x).charpoly = minpoly K x := by
  have hdvd : minpoly K x ∣ (Algebra.lmul K E x).charpoly :=
    minpoly.dvd K x (Algebra.aeval_self_charpoly_lmul x)
  apply Polynomial.eq_of_monic_of_dvd_of_natDegree_le
    (minpoly.monic (IsIntegral.of_finite K x)) (charpoly_monic _) hdvd
  rw [charpoly_natDegree, hDeg]

end Primitive

end LinearMap

-- Author: @toskua, Avocado
module

public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Charpoly.ToMatrix
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.Charpoly.Basic
public import Mathlib.RingTheory.LocalRing.Quotient

/-!
# Characteristic polynomials under quotient and base-ring equivalence

* `Algebra.charpoly_lmul_quotient_maximalIdeal_map`: over a local
  ring `R`, the characteristic polynomial of left multiplication by the
  class of `s` on the special fiber `S ⧸ 𝔪S` is the reduction modulo
  `𝔪` of the characteristic polynomial of left multiplication by `s`
  on `S`.
* `Algebra.charpoly_lmul_map_ringEquiv`: if the scalars of an
  algebra are reindexed along a ring equivalence `φ : k ≃+* k'`, the
  characteristic polynomial of left multiplication is mapped along
  `φ`.

Both proofs compare matrices in corresponding bases: the reduced basis
`IsLocalRing.basisQuotient` in the first case, and the transferred
basis `Module.Basis.mapCoeffs` (the same vectors, with coordinates
reindexed along `φ.symm`) in the second; in each case the matrices
differ entrywise by the relevant ring homomorphism and
`Matrix.charpoly_map` concludes.

The freeness and finiteness instances needed to *form* the
characteristic polynomials in the statements are not automatic (the
quotient module is free only because `basisQuotient` is a basis, and
finiteness over the reindexed scalars only because a transferred basis
is still finite), so they are supplied explicitly by `let` in the
statements from those bases.  Both classes are propositions, so clients
whose context provides different instance terms can still apply the
lemmas up to defeq.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false

open Polynomial

namespace Algebra

section QuotientMaximalIdeal

variable {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
  [IsLocalRing R] [Module.Finite R S] [Module.Free R S]

/-- Quotient base-change for the characteristic polynomial of left
multiplication: over a local ring `R` with maximal ideal `𝔪`,
the characteristic polynomial of left multiplication by the class of
`s` on `S ⧸ 𝔪S` over the residue field `R ⧸ 𝔪` is the reduction
modulo `𝔪` of the characteristic polynomial of left multiplication by
`s` on `S`. -/
theorem charpoly_lmul_quotient_maximalIdeal_map (s : S) :
    let _ : Module.Free (R ⧸ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)
        (S ⧸ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R S)) :=
      Module.Free.of_basis (IsLocalRing.basisQuotient
        (Module.Free.chooseBasis R S))
    let _ : Module.Finite (R ⧸ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)
        (S ⧸ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R S)) :=
      Module.Finite.of_basis (IsLocalRing.basisQuotient
        (Module.Free.chooseBasis R S))
    (Algebra.lmul (R ⧸ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)
        (S ⧸ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R S))
        (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ s)).charpoly
      = (Algebra.lmul R S s).charpoly.map
          (Ideal.Quotient.mk (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)) := by
  classical
  let b := Module.Free.chooseBasis R S
  have _ : Module.Free (R ⧸ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)
      (S ⧸ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R S)) :=
    Module.Free.of_basis (IsLocalRing.basisQuotient b)
  have _ : Module.Finite (R ⧸ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)
      (S ⧸ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R S)) :=
    Module.Finite.of_basis (IsLocalRing.basisQuotient b)
  have hmat : LinearMap.toMatrix (IsLocalRing.basisQuotient b)
        (IsLocalRing.basisQuotient b)
        (Algebra.lmul (R ⧸ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)
          (S ⧸ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R S))
          (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ s))
      = (LinearMap.toMatrix b b (Algebra.lmul R S s)).map
          (Ideal.Quotient.mk (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)) := by
    ext i j
    rw [LinearMap.toMatrix_apply, Matrix.map_apply,
      LinearMap.toMatrix_apply, IsLocalRing.basisQuotient_apply]
    have hmul : (Algebra.lmul (R ⧸ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)
          (S ⧸ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R S))
          (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ s)) (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (b j))
        = Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (s * b j) := by
      simp [Algebra.coe_lmul_eq_mul]
    rw [hmul, IsLocalRing.basisQuotient_repr]
    simp [Algebra.coe_lmul_eq_mul]
  change (Algebra.lmul (R ⧸ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)
        (S ⧸ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R S))
        (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ s)).charpoly
      = (Algebra.lmul R S s).charpoly.map
          (Ideal.Quotient.mk (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R))
  rw [← LinearMap.charpoly_toMatrix _ (IsLocalRing.basisQuotient b),
    ← LinearMap.charpoly_toMatrix _ b, hmat, Matrix.charpoly_map]

end QuotientMaximalIdeal

section MapRingEquiv

variable {k k' E : Type*} [Field k] [Field k'] [CommRing E]
  [Algebra k' E] [Module.Finite k' E]

/-- Characteristic polynomial of left multiplication under a base-ring
equivalence: if `E` is viewed as a `k`-algebra along
`φ : k ≃+* k'`, then mapping the `k`-characteristic polynomial of left
multiplication by `x` along `φ` gives the `k'`-characteristic
polynomial of left multiplication by `x`. -/
theorem charpoly_lmul_map_ringEquiv (φ : k ≃+* k') (x : E) :
    letI : Algebra k E :=
      ((algebraMap k' E).comp φ.toRingHom).toAlgebra
    let _ : Module.Finite k E :=
      Module.Finite.of_basis ((Module.finBasis k' E).mapCoeffs φ.symm
        (fun c y => by
          have hmap : algebraMap k E
              = (algebraMap k' E).comp φ.toRingHom := rfl
          simp only [hmap, Algebra.smul_def, RingHom.comp_apply]
          change algebraMap k' E (φ (φ.symm c)) * y
            = algebraMap k' E c * y
          rw [RingEquiv.apply_symm_apply]))
    (Algebra.lmul k E x).charpoly.map φ.toRingHom
      = (Algebra.lmul k' E x).charpoly := by
  classical
  let _ : Algebra k E :=
    ((algebraMap k' E).comp φ.toRingHom).toAlgebra
  have hsmul : ∀ (c : k) (y : E), c • y = φ c • y := fun c y => by
    have hmap : algebraMap k E
        = (algebraMap k' E).comp φ.toRingHom := rfl
    simp only [hmap, Algebra.smul_def, RingHom.comp_apply]
    rfl
  let b := Module.finBasis k' E
  let b' := b.mapCoeffs φ.symm (fun c y => by
    simpa only [RingEquiv.apply_symm_apply] using hsmul (φ.symm c) y)
  have _ : Module.Finite k E :=
    Module.Finite.of_basis b'
  have hmat : LinearMap.toMatrix b'
        b' (Algebra.lmul k E x)
      = (LinearMap.toMatrix b b (Algebra.lmul k' E x)).map
          φ.symm.toRingHom := by
    ext i j
    rw [LinearMap.toMatrix_apply, Matrix.map_apply,
      LinearMap.toMatrix_apply]
    simp only [b', Module.Basis.mapCoeffs_apply, Module.Basis.mapCoeffs_repr,
      Algebra.coe_lmul_eq_mul]
    rfl
  have key : (Algebra.lmul k E x).charpoly
      = (Algebra.lmul k' E x).charpoly.map φ.symm.toRingHom := by
    rw [← LinearMap.charpoly_toMatrix _ b',
      ← LinearMap.charpoly_toMatrix _ b, hmat, Matrix.charpoly_map]
  have hcomp : φ.toRingHom.comp φ.symm.toRingHom = RingHom.id k' := by
    ext a
    simp
  change (Algebra.lmul k E x).charpoly.map φ.toRingHom
    = (Algebra.lmul k' E x).charpoly
  rw [key, Polynomial.map_map, hcomp, Polynomial.map_id]

end MapRingEquiv

end Algebra

-- Author: @toskua, Avocado
module

public import MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.Charpoly.DependentPi

/-!
# Characteristic polynomials of left multiplication in a tower

For a tower of finite extensions of fields `k ⊆ F ⊆ E` and an element
`θ₀ : F` of the intermediate field, left multiplication on `E` by the
image of `θ₀` has characteristic polynomial over `k` equal to the
`Module.finrank F E`-th power of the characteristic polynomial of left
multiplication by `θ₀` on `F`:

```text
(Algebra.lmul k E (algebraMap F E θ₀)).charpoly
  = (Algebra.lmul k F θ₀).charpoly ^ Module.finrank F E.
```

This is leaf `B8` of the weighted branch multiplicity proof tree: for a
normalization branch, `F` is the residue field of the reduced place,
`θ₀` is the class of `X` (a primitive element of `F` over `k`, whose
characteristic polynomial on `F` over `k` is its minimal polynomial over
`k`), and `E` is the full
branch residue field, so the characteristic polynomial of the reduced
root is a power of its minimal polynomial with exponent the relative
residue degree.

## Informal proof

Choose an `F`-basis of `E` indexed by `Fin (Module.finrank F E)`
(`Module.finBasis`).  The coordinate equivalence `Module.Basis.equivFun`
identifies `E` with `Fin (finrank F E) → F` as `F`-modules, hence also
as `k`-modules after restricting scalars.  Multiplication by
`algebraMap F E θ₀` is the scalar action of `θ₀` on `E` as an
`F`-module, so in coordinates it acts componentwise as multiplication
by `θ₀` on `F` — the matrix is block-diagonal with `finrank F E`
identical blocks.  Conjugation invariance of the characteristic
polynomial and the dependent-product formula
`LinearMap.charpoly_pi_dependent` then give a product of
`finrank F E` copies of `(Algebra.lmul k F θ₀).charpoly`.

Only the bottom two entries of the tower need to be fields: `E` may be
any ring with compatible algebra structures.  The finiteness of `E`
over `k` is listed separately because the statement's characteristic
polynomial needs it; it follows from the other two finiteness
assumptions.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false

open Polynomial

namespace Algebra

section Tower

variable {k F E : Type*} [Field k] [Field F] [Ring E]
  [Algebra k F] [Algebra F E] [Algebra k E] [IsScalarTower k F E]
  [FiniteDimensional k F] [FiniteDimensional F E] [FiniteDimensional k E]

/-- Characteristic polynomial of left multiplication by an
intermediate-field element in a finite tower: if `θ₀` lies in the
intermediate field `F`, the characteristic polynomial of left
multiplication by its image in `E` is the `Module.finrank F E`-th power
of the characteristic polynomial of left multiplication by `θ₀` on
`F`. -/
theorem lmul_charpoly_algebraMap_tower (θ₀ : F) :
    (Algebra.lmul k E (algebraMap F E θ₀)).charpoly =
      (Algebra.lmul k F θ₀).charpoly ^ Module.finrank F E := by
  classical
  let n := Module.finrank F E
  let b : Module.Basis (Fin n) F E := Module.finBasis F E
  let e : E ≃ₗ[k] (Fin n → F) := b.equivFun.restrictScalars k
  have he : ∀ x i, e x i = b.repr x i := fun x i =>
    congrFun (Module.Basis.equivFun_apply b x) i
  have hconj : e.conj (Algebra.lmul k E (algebraMap F E θ₀)) =
      LinearMap.pi
        (fun i => (Algebra.lmul k F θ₀).comp (LinearMap.proj i)) := by
    apply LinearMap.ext
    intro y
    obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := e.surjective y
    funext i
    simp only [LinearEquiv.conj_apply_apply,
      LinearEquiv.symm_apply_apply, LinearMap.pi_apply,
      LinearMap.comp_apply, LinearMap.proj_apply, he]
    have hmul : (Algebra.lmul k E (algebraMap F E θ₀)) x = θ₀ • x := by
      simp only [Algebra.coe_lmul_eq_mul, LinearMap.mul_apply',
        Algebra.smul_def]
    rw [hmul, map_smul, Finsupp.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]
    simp only [Algebra.coe_lmul_eq_mul, LinearMap.mul_apply']
  calc
    (Algebra.lmul k E (algebraMap F E θ₀)).charpoly =
        (e.conj (Algebra.lmul k E (algebraMap F E θ₀))).charpoly :=
      (LinearEquiv.charpoly_conj e _).symm
    _ = ∏ _i : Fin n, (Algebra.lmul k F θ₀).charpoly := by
      rw [hconj, LinearMap.charpoly_pi_dependent]
    _ = (Algebra.lmul k F θ₀).charpoly ^ n := by simp
    _ = (Algebra.lmul k F θ₀).charpoly ^ Module.finrank F E := rfl

end Tower

end Algebra

-- Author: @toskua
module

public import Mathlib.RingTheory.Length
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Quotient.Basic
public import Mathlib.Algebra.Exact.Basic

/-!
# Length of the literal cokernel of a composite

The quotient maps are induced by the actual linear maps. If the second map
is injective, its induced map from the first cokernel is injective and the
next quotient map is surjective. Their exact sequence earns the length sum
without any finite-length premise. This is a prerequisite for determinant
length and arbitrary-source norm orders over singular one-dimensional rings.
-/

@[expose] public section
noncomputable section

universe u v w z

namespace LinearMap

variable {R : Type u} [Ring R]
variable {M : Type v} {N : Type w} {P : Type z}
variable [AddCommGroup M] [AddCommGroup N] [AddCommGroup P]
variable [Module R M] [Module R N] [Module R P]

private def cokerCompLeft (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (g : N →ₗ[R] P) :
    N ⧸ f.range →ₗ[R] P ⧸ (g.comp f).range :=
  f.range.mapQ (g.comp f).range g (by
    rintro n ⟨m, rfl⟩
    exact ⟨m, rfl⟩)

private def cokerCompRight (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (g : N →ₗ[R] P) :
    P ⧸ (g.comp f).range →ₗ[R] P ⧸ g.range :=
  (g.comp f).range.mapQ g.range LinearMap.id (by
    rintro p ⟨m, rfl⟩
    exact ⟨f m, rfl⟩)

/-- An injective second map earns the full cokernel-length composition law.
The literal quotient modules may have infinite length or nilpotent scalar
actions; neither finite length nor a determinant/order equality is assumed. -/
theorem length_coker_comp_of_injective (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (g : N →ₗ[R] P)
    (hg : Function.Injective g) :
    Module.length R (P ⧸ (g.comp f).range) =
      Module.length R (N ⧸ f.range) + Module.length R (P ⧸ g.range) := by
  let i := cokerCompLeft f g
  let j := cokerCompRight f g
  have hi : Function.Injective i := by
    rw [injective_iff_map_eq_zero]
    intro q hq
    obtain ⟨n, rfl⟩ := Submodule.mkQ_surjective f.range q
    change (g.comp f).range.mkQ (g n) = 0 at hq
    rw [Submodule.mkQ_apply, Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero] at hq
    obtain ⟨m, hm⟩ := hq
    rw [Submodule.mkQ_apply, Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero]
    exact ⟨m, hg hm⟩
  have hj : Function.Surjective j := by
    intro q
    obtain ⟨p, rfl⟩ := Submodule.mkQ_surjective g.range q
    exact ⟨(g.comp f).range.mkQ p, rfl⟩
  have hseq : Function.Exact i j := by
    intro q
    obtain ⟨p, rfl⟩ := Submodule.mkQ_surjective (g.comp f).range q
    constructor
    · intro hp
      change g.range.mkQ p = 0 at hp
      rw [Submodule.mkQ_apply, Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero] at hp
      obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := hp
      refine ⟨f.range.mkQ n, ?_⟩
      change (g.comp f).range.mkQ (g n) = (g.comp f).range.mkQ p
      rw [hn]
    · rintro ⟨q, hq⟩
      rw [← hq]
      obtain ⟨n, rfl⟩ := Submodule.mkQ_surjective f.range q
      change g.range.mkQ (g n) = 0
      rw [Submodule.mkQ_apply, Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero]
      exact ⟨n, rfl⟩
  exact Module.length_eq_add_of_exact i j hi hj hseq

private def upperBlockMap (f : M →ₗ[R] M) (r : N →ₗ[R] M) (g : N →ₗ[R] N) :
    M × N →ₗ[R] M × N :=
  (f.comp (LinearMap.fst R M N) + r.comp (LinearMap.snd R M N)).prod
    (g.comp (LinearMap.snd R M N))

/-- A genuine upper block map has the sum of its diagonal cokernel
lengths when its lower diagonal map is injective. The full quotient modules
and arbitrary off-diagonal map are retained; no finite length is assumed. -/
theorem length_coker_upper_block_of_injective
    (f : M →ₗ[R] M) (r : N →ₗ[R] M) (g : N →ₗ[R] N) (hg : Function.Injective g) :
    Module.length R ((M × N) ⧸
        ((f.comp (LinearMap.fst R M N) + r.comp (LinearMap.snd R M N)).prod
          (g.comp (LinearMap.snd R M N))).range) =
      Module.length R (M ⧸ f.range) + Module.length R (N ⧸ g.range) := by
  let T := upperBlockMap f r g
  let i : M ⧸ f.range →ₗ[R] (M × N) ⧸ T.range :=
    f.range.mapQ T.range (LinearMap.inl R M N) (by
      rintro m ⟨a, rfl⟩
      refine ⟨(a, 0), ?_⟩
      change (f a + r 0, g 0) = (f a, 0)
      rw [map_zero, map_zero, add_zero])
  let j : (M × N) ⧸ T.range →ₗ[R] N ⧸ g.range :=
    T.range.mapQ g.range (LinearMap.snd R M N) (by
      rintro p ⟨q, rfl⟩
      exact ⟨q.2, rfl⟩)
  have hi : Function.Injective i := by
    rw [injective_iff_map_eq_zero]
    intro q hq
    obtain ⟨m, rfl⟩ := Submodule.mkQ_surjective f.range q
    change T.range.mkQ (m, 0) = 0 at hq
    rw [Submodule.mkQ_apply, Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero] at hq
    obtain ⟨⟨a, b⟩, hab⟩ := hq
    have hb0 : g b = 0 := congrArg Prod.snd hab
    have hb : b = 0 := hg (hb0.trans g.map_zero.symm)
    have ha : f a + r b = m := congrArg Prod.fst hab
    rw [hb, map_zero, add_zero] at ha
    rw [Submodule.mkQ_apply, Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero]
    exact ⟨a, ha⟩
  have hj : Function.Surjective j := by
    intro q
    obtain ⟨n, rfl⟩ := Submodule.mkQ_surjective g.range q
    exact ⟨T.range.mkQ (0, n), rfl⟩
  have hseq : Function.Exact i j := by
    intro q
    obtain ⟨⟨m, n⟩, rfl⟩ := Submodule.mkQ_surjective T.range q
    constructor
    · intro hn
      change g.range.mkQ n = 0 at hn
      rw [Submodule.mkQ_apply, Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero] at hn
      obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := hn
      refine ⟨f.range.mkQ (m - r b), ?_⟩
      change T.range.mkQ (m - r b, 0) = T.range.mkQ (m, n)
      rw [Submodule.mkQ_apply, Submodule.mkQ_apply, Submodule.Quotient.eq]
      refine ⟨(0, -b), ?_⟩
      change (f 0 + r (-b), g (-b)) = (m - r b, 0) - (m, n)
      ext <;> simp [hb]
    · rintro ⟨q, hq⟩
      rw [← hq]
      obtain ⟨m, rfl⟩ := Submodule.mkQ_surjective f.range q
      change g.range.mkQ 0 = 0
      exact map_zero _
  exact Module.length_eq_add_of_exact i j hi hj hseq

/-- An actual change of basis in the domain leaves the literal image
submodule and hence the full quotient cokernel length unchanged. -/
theorem length_coker_precompose_equiv (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (e : P ≃ₗ[R] M) :
    Module.length R (N ⧸ (f.comp e.toLinearMap).range) = Module.length R (N ⧸ f.range) := by
  have hr : (f.comp e.toLinearMap).range = f.range := by
    ext n
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨p, rfl⟩
      exact ⟨e p, rfl⟩
    · rintro ⟨m, rfl⟩
      exact ⟨e.symm m, by simp⟩
  exact congrArg (fun Q : Submodule R N => Module.length R (N ⧸ Q)) hr

/-- An actual change of basis in the codomain transports the full
cokernel without changing its length, including infinite-length cases. -/
theorem length_coker_postcompose_equiv (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (e : N ≃ₗ[R] P) :
    Module.length R (P ⧸ (e.toLinearMap.comp f).range) = Module.length R (N ⧸ f.range) := by
  have hz : Module.length R (P ⧸ e.toLinearMap.range) = 0 := by
    rw [LinearMap.range_eq_top.mpr e.surjective]
    exact Module.length_eq_zero
  have h := length_coker_comp_of_injective f e.toLinearMap e.injective
  rw [hz, add_zero] at h
  exact h

end LinearMap

-- Author: @toskua
module

public import MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.CokernelLengthComposition

/-!
# Literal pivot elimination on arbitrary module blocks

The pivot is nonzero, with no unit-pivot premise. The actual elimination map
and Schur map retain the original off-diagonal maps. Their composition and
injectivity are earned from the actual module operations. These are the
arbitrary-size prerequisites for singular determinant/cokernel length.
-/

@[expose] public section
noncomputable section

universe u v

namespace LinearMap

variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {N : Type v} [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]

/-- The original pivot block acting on the full module R × N. -/
def pivotBlock (a : R) (r : N →ₗ[R] R) (c : R →ₗ[R] N) (B : N →ₗ[R] N) :
    R × N →ₗ[R] R × N :=
  (a • LinearMap.fst R R N + r.comp (LinearMap.snd R R N)).prod
    (c.comp (LinearMap.fst R R N) + B.comp (LinearMap.snd R R N))

/-- The literal lower elimination map, with the original nonunit pivot. -/
def pivotElimination (a : R) (c : R →ₗ[R] N) : R × N →ₗ[R] R × N :=
  (LinearMap.fst R R N).prod
    (-(c.comp (LinearMap.fst R R N)) + a • LinearMap.snd R R N)

/-- The actual Schur block; the full original off-diagonal product remains. -/
def pivotSchur (a : R) (r : N →ₗ[R] R) (c : R →ₗ[R] N) (B : N →ₗ[R] N) : N →ₗ[R] N :=
  a • B - c.comp r

/-- Actual pivot elimination produces the original upper block map with
the full Schur block, without inverting the pivot. -/
theorem pivotElimination_comp (a : R) (r : N →ₗ[R] R) (c : R →ₗ[R] N) (B : N →ₗ[R] N) :
    (pivotElimination a c).comp (pivotBlock a r c B) =
      (a • LinearMap.fst R R N + r.comp (LinearMap.snd R R N)).prod
        ((pivotSchur a r c B).comp (LinearMap.snd R R N)) := by
  apply LinearMap.ext
  rintro ⟨x, y⟩
  apply Prod.ext
  · rfl
  · change -(c (a * x + r y)) + a • (c x + B y) = a • B y - c (r y)
    have hc : c (a * x) = a • c x := c.map_smul a x
    rw [map_add, hc, smul_add]
    abel

/-- A nonzero pivot earns injectivity of the actual elimination map on
every torsion-free module; a unit or finite-rank premise is unnecessary. -/
theorem pivotElimination_injective [NoZeroSMulDivisors R N] (a : R) (ha : a ≠ 0)
    (c : R →ₗ[R] N) : Function.Injective (pivotElimination a c) := by
  rw [injective_iff_map_eq_zero]
  rintro ⟨x, y⟩ h
  have hx : x = 0 := congrArg Prod.fst h
  have hy : -(c x) + a • y = 0 := congrArg Prod.snd h
  rw [hx, map_zero, neg_zero, zero_add] at hy
  have hy0 : y = 0 := (eq_zero_or_eq_zero_of_smul_eq_zero hy).resolve_left ha
  exact Prod.ext hx hy0

/-- Injectivity of the original block and its nonzero pivot earns the full
Schur block's injectivity by clearing that pivot in the actual source vector. -/
theorem pivotSchur_injective [NoZeroSMulDivisors R N]
    (a : R) (ha : a ≠ 0) (r : N →ₗ[R] R) (c : R →ₗ[R] N) (B : N →ₗ[R] N)
    (hA : Function.Injective (pivotBlock a r c B)) : Function.Injective (pivotSchur a r c B) := by
  rw [injective_iff_map_eq_zero]
  intro y hy
  have hzero : pivotBlock a r c B (-r y, a • y) = 0 := by
    apply Prod.ext
    · change a * (-r y) + r (a • y) = 0
      rw [map_smul]
      simp
    · change c (-r y) + B (a • y) = 0
      rw [map_neg, map_smul]
      have hs : a • B y = c (r y) := sub_eq_zero.mp hy
      rw [hs, neg_add_cancel]
  have hv : (-r y, a • y) = (0, 0) := hA (hzero.trans (pivotBlock a r c B).map_zero.symm)
  have hy0 : a • y = 0 := congrArg Prod.snd hv
  exact (eq_zero_or_eq_zero_of_smul_eq_zero hy0).resolve_left ha

/-- The actual elimination map has precisely the full cokernel length of
its lower scalar block. The proof uses actual product changes of basis and
the upper block exact sequence, retaining nonunit pivots. -/
theorem length_coker_pivotElimination (a : R) (c : R →ₗ[R] N) :
    Module.length R ((R × N) ⧸ (pivotElimination a c).range) =
      Module.length R (N ⧸ (a • (LinearMap.id : N →ₗ[R] N)).range) := by
  let e := LinearEquiv.prodComm R R N
  let E := pivotElimination a c
  let H : N × R →ₗ[R] N × R :=
    ((a • (LinearMap.id : N →ₗ[R] N)).comp (LinearMap.fst R N R) +
      (-c).comp (LinearMap.snd R N R)).prod (LinearMap.snd R N R)
  have he : (e.toLinearMap.comp E).comp e.symm.toLinearMap = H := by
    apply LinearMap.ext
    rintro ⟨y, x⟩
    apply Prod.ext
    · change -c x + a • y = a • y + -c x
      exact add_comm _ _
    · rfl
  have hpost := length_coker_postcompose_equiv E e
  have hpre := length_coker_precompose_equiv (e.toLinearMap.comp E) e.symm
  have hchange : Module.length R ((R × N) ⧸ E.range) =
      Module.length R ((N × R) ⧸ H.range) := by
    rw [he] at hpre
    exact hpost.symm.trans hpre.symm
  have hblock := length_coker_upper_block_of_injective
    (a • (LinearMap.id : N →ₗ[R] N)) (-c) (LinearMap.id : R →ₗ[R] R)
    (fun x y h => h)
  have hzero : Module.length R (R ⧸ (LinearMap.id : R →ₗ[R] R).range) = 0 := by
    rw [LinearMap.range_eq_top.mpr Function.surjective_id]
    exact Module.length_eq_zero
  rw [hzero, add_zero] at hblock
  exact hchange.trans hblock

/-- Full pivot elimination earns the all-module cokernel length relation
needed by determinant induction. Injectivity is derived for the actual
elimination and Schur maps; no finite-length or norm/order equality premise
is introduced. -/
theorem length_coker_pivot_relation [NoZeroSMulDivisors R N]
    (a : R) (ha : a ≠ 0) (r : N →ₗ[R] R) (c : R →ₗ[R] N) (B : N →ₗ[R] N)
    (hA : Function.Injective (pivotBlock a r c B)) :
    Module.length R ((R × N) ⧸ (pivotBlock a r c B).range) +
        Module.length R (N ⧸ (a • (LinearMap.id : N →ₗ[R] N)).range) =
      Module.length R (R ⧸ (a • (LinearMap.id : R →ₗ[R] R)).range) +
        Module.length R (N ⧸ (pivotSchur a r c B).range) := by
  have hcomp := length_coker_comp_of_injective (pivotBlock a r c B) (pivotElimination a c)
    (pivotElimination_injective a ha c)
  rw [length_coker_pivotElimination a c] at hcomp
  have hs := pivotSchur_injective a ha r c B hA
  have hupper := length_coker_upper_block_of_injective
    (a • (LinearMap.id : R →ₗ[R] R)) r (pivotSchur a r c B) hs
  have hproduct : (pivotElimination a c).comp (pivotBlock a r c B) =
      ((a • (LinearMap.id : R →ₗ[R] R)).comp (LinearMap.fst R R N) +
        r.comp (LinearMap.snd R R N)).prod ((pivotSchur a r c B).comp (LinearMap.snd R R N)) :=
    pivotElimination_comp a r c B
  rw [hproduct] at hcomp
  exact hcomp.symm.trans hupper

end LinearMap
