module

public import MathlibExt.FieldTheory.Galois.TensorProductDecomposition
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Complex.FiniteDimensional
public import Mathlib.Analysis.Complex.Polynomial.Basic
public import Mathlib.Algebra.Ring.Fin
public import Mathlib.Tactic.FinCases
public import Mathlib.Tactic.NormNum
public import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring

/-!
# The original complex tensor over the reals

The canonical finite-Galois self-tensor equivalence is reindexed by the
actual identity and conjugation automorphisms of `ℂ/ℝ`. Its algebra
structure retains `(z * w, z * conj w)` and the original twisted right action.
-/

@[expose] public section
noncomputable section

open TensorProduct
open scoped ComplexConjugate

namespace Complex

private theorem realTensorIdentity_ne_conjugation :
    ((AlgEquiv.refl : ℂ ≃ₐ[ℝ] ℂ)) ≠ Complex.conjAe := by
  intro h
  have hI := congrArg (fun e : ℂ ≃ₐ[ℝ] ℂ => (e Complex.I).im) h
  norm_num at hI

/-- Number the actual real algebra automorphisms by identity and conjugation. -/
def realTensorAutomorphismIndex : Fin 2 ≃ (ℂ ≃ₐ[ℝ] ℂ) :=
  Equiv.ofBijective
    (fun j => if j = 0 then (AlgEquiv.refl : ℂ ≃ₐ[ℝ] ℂ) else Complex.conjAe) (by
      constructor
      · intro i j h
        fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
          simp_all [realTensorIdentity_ne_conjugation, Ne.symm realTensorIdentity_ne_conjugation]
      · intro σ
        rcases Complex.real_algHom_eq_id_or_conj σ.toAlgHom with h | h
        · refine ⟨0, ?_⟩
          ext z
          exact (DFunLike.congr_fun h z).symm
        · refine ⟨1, ?_⟩
          ext z
          exact (DFunLike.congr_fun h z).symm)

/-- The actual finite-Galois tensor decomposition retains its full complex algebra structure. -/
def tensorProductRealAlgEquiv :
    letI : Module ℝ ℂ := Complex.ofRealHom.toModule
    letI : Algebra ℝ ℂ := Complex.ofRealHom.toAlgebra
    (ℂ ⊗[ℝ] ℂ) ≃ₐ[ℂ] ℂ × ℂ := by
  letI : Module ℝ ℂ := Complex.ofRealHom.toModule
  letI : Algebra ℝ ℂ := Complex.ofRealHom.toAlgebra
  letI : IsAlgClosure ℝ ℂ :=
    { isAlgClosed := Complex.isAlgClosed
      isAlgebraic := inferInstance }
  exact (MilnorK.finiteGaloisTensorProductEquiv ℝ ℂ).trans
    ((AlgEquiv.piCongrLeft' ℂ (fun _ : ℂ ≃ₐ[ℝ] ℂ => ℂ)
      realTensorAutomorphismIndex.symm).trans
      (AlgEquiv.ofRingEquiv (f := RingEquiv.piFinTwo (fun _ : Fin 2 => ℂ)) (by
        intro z
        rfl)))

/-- The same original pure tensor has its identity and conjugation coordinates. -/
@[simp]
theorem tensorProductRealAlgEquiv_tmul (z w : ℂ) :
    letI : Module ℝ ℂ := Complex.ofRealHom.toModule
    letI : Algebra ℝ ℂ := Complex.ofRealHom.toAlgebra
    tensorProductRealAlgEquiv (z ⊗ₜ[ℝ] w) = (z * w, z * conj w) := by
  let : Module ℝ ℂ := Complex.ofRealHom.toModule
  let : Algebra ℝ ℂ := Complex.ofRealHom.toAlgebra
  let : IsAlgClosure ℝ ℂ :=
    { isAlgClosed := Complex.isAlgClosed
      isAlgebraic := inferInstance }
  apply Prod.ext
  · change MilnorK.finiteGaloisTensorProductEquiv ℝ ℂ (z ⊗ₜ[ℝ] w)
      (realTensorAutomorphismIndex 0) = z * w
    rw [MilnorK.finiteGaloisTensorProductEquiv_tmul]
    rfl
  · change MilnorK.finiteGaloisTensorProductEquiv ℝ ℂ (z ⊗ₜ[ℝ] w)
      (realTensorAutomorphismIndex 1) = z * conj w
    rw [MilnorK.finiteGaloisTensorProductEquiv_tmul]
    rfl

/-- Additive coercion of the same canonical algebra equivalence. -/
def tensorProductRealAddEquiv :
    letI : Module ℝ ℂ := Complex.ofRealHom.toModule
    letI : Algebra ℝ ℂ := Complex.ofRealHom.toAlgebra
    (ℂ ⊗[ℝ] ℂ) ≃+ ℂ × ℂ :=
  tensorProductRealAlgEquiv.toAddEquiv

/-- The additive coercion retains the original pure tensor coordinates. -/
@[simp]
theorem tensorProductRealAddEquiv_tmul (z w : ℂ) :
    letI : Module ℝ ℂ := Complex.ofRealHom.toModule
    letI : Algebra ℝ ℂ := Complex.ofRealHom.toAlgebra
    tensorProductRealAddEquiv (z ⊗ₜ[ℝ] w) = (z * w, z * conj w) :=
  tensorProductRealAlgEquiv_tmul z w

/-- The original field K₀ client uses the actual complex-linear coercion. -/
def tensorProductRealEquiv :
    letI : Module ℝ ℂ := Complex.ofRealHom.toModule
    letI : Algebra ℝ ℂ := Complex.ofRealHom.toAlgebra
    (ℂ ⊗[ℝ] ℂ) ≃ₗ[ℂ] ℂ × ℂ :=
  tensorProductRealAlgEquiv.toLinearEquiv

/-- The complex-linear coercion retains the original pure tensor map. -/
@[simp]
theorem tensorProductRealEquiv_tmul (z w : ℂ) :
    letI : Module ℝ ℂ := Complex.ofRealHom.toModule
    letI : Algebra ℝ ℂ := Complex.ofRealHom.toAlgebra
    tensorProductRealEquiv (z ⊗ₜ[ℝ] w) = (z * w, z * conj w) :=
  tensorProductRealAlgEquiv_tmul z w

/-- The whole original inverse is verified against the same canonical coordinate map. -/
theorem tensorProductRealEquiv_symm_apply (p : ℂ × ℂ) :
    letI : Module ℝ ℂ := Complex.ofRealHom.toModule
    letI : Algebra ℝ ℂ := Complex.ofRealHom.toAlgebra
    tensorProductRealEquiv.symm p =
      ((p.1 + p.2) * (1 / 2 : ℂ)) ⊗ₜ[ℝ] (1 : ℂ) +
        ((p.1 - p.2) * (-Complex.I * (1 / 2 : ℂ))) ⊗ₜ[ℝ] Complex.I := by
  let : Module ℝ ℂ := Complex.ofRealHom.toModule
  let : Algebra ℝ ℂ := Complex.ofRealHom.toAlgebra
  apply tensorProductRealEquiv.injective
  rw [tensorProductRealEquiv.apply_symm_apply, map_add,
    tensorProductRealEquiv_tmul, tensorProductRealEquiv_tmul]
  apply Prod.ext <;> simp only [Prod.fst_add, Prod.snd_add, map_one, mul_one, conj_I]
  all_goals
    ring_nf
    simp [Complex.I_sq]
    ring

/-- Algebra multiplicativity gives the same twisted action on every original tensor. -/
theorem tensorProductRealEquiv_right_action :
    letI : Module ℝ ℂ := Complex.ofRealHom.toModule
    letI : Algebra ℝ ℂ := Complex.ofRealHom.toAlgebra
    ∀ (t : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] ℂ) (s : ℂ),
      tensorProductRealEquiv (t * (1 ⊗ₜ[ℝ] s)) =
        ((tensorProductRealEquiv t).1 * s, (tensorProductRealEquiv t).2 * conj s) := by
  let : Module ℝ ℂ := Complex.ofRealHom.toModule
  let : Algebra ℝ ℂ := Complex.ofRealHom.toAlgebra
  intro t s
  change tensorProductRealAlgEquiv (t * (1 ⊗ₜ[ℝ] s)) =
    ((tensorProductRealAlgEquiv t).1 * s, (tensorProductRealAlgEquiv t).2 * conj s)
  rw [map_mul, tensorProductRealAlgEquiv_tmul]
  simp only [one_mul, Prod.mul_def]

end Complex

end

module

public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.DFinsupp

/-!
# Linear maps into dependent finitely supported functions

A family of linear maps f i : M →ₗ[R] N i determines a linear map into the
dependent direct sum whenever its value on every input has finite support.
This file packages that standard construction and exposes its coordinate
formula.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
noncomputable section

universe uR uι uM uN

namespace DFinsupp

variable {R : Type uR} [Semiring R]
variable {ι : Type uι}
variable {M : Type uM} [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M]
variable {N : ι → Type uN}
variable [∀ i, AddCommMonoid (N i)] [∀ i, Module R (N i)]

/-- Assemble a pointwise finitely supported family of linear maps into one
linear map with dependent direct-sum target. -/
noncomputable def linearMapOfFiniteSupport
    (f : ∀ i, M →ₗ[R] N i)
    (hf : ∀ x, {i | f i x ≠ 0}.Finite) :
    M →ₗ[R] Π₀ i, N i := by
  classical
  let toFunImpl (x : M) : Π₀ i, N i :=
    DFinsupp.mk (hf x).toFinset fun i => f i.1 x
  have applyImpl (x : M) (i : ι) : toFunImpl x i = f i x := by
    by_cases hi : i ∈ (hf x).toFinset
    · exact DFinsupp.mk_of_mem hi
    · rw [DFinsupp.mk_of_notMem hi]
      by_contra h
      exact hi ((hf x).mem_toFinset.mpr (Ne.symm h))
  exact
    { toFun := toFunImpl
      map_add' := by
        intro x y
        apply DFinsupp.ext
        intro i
        calc
          toFunImpl (x + y) i = f i (x + y) := applyImpl _ _
          _ = f i x + f i y := map_add _ _ _
          _ = toFunImpl x i + toFunImpl y i := by
            rw [applyImpl, applyImpl]
          _ = (toFunImpl x + toFunImpl y) i := rfl
      map_smul' := by
        intro c x
        apply DFinsupp.ext
        intro i
        calc
          toFunImpl (c • x) i = f i (c • x) := applyImpl _ _
          _ = c • f i x := map_smul _ _ _
          _ = c • toFunImpl x i := by rw [applyImpl]
          _ = (c • toFunImpl x) i := rfl }

/-- Coordinate evaluation of the finite-support linear-map constructor. -/
@[simp]
theorem linearMapOfFiniteSupport_apply
    (f : ∀ i, M →ₗ[R] N i)
    (hf : ∀ x, {i | f i x ≠ 0}.Finite)
    (x : M) (i : ι) :
    linearMapOfFiniteSupport f hf x i = f i x := by
  classical
  unfold linearMapOfFiniteSupport
  dsimp only
  change (DFinsupp.mk (hf x).toFinset
    (fun j => f j.1 x)) i = f i x
  by_cases hi : i ∈ (hf x).toFinset
  · exact DFinsupp.mk_of_mem hi
  · rw [DFinsupp.mk_of_notMem hi]
    by_contra h
    exact hi ((hf x).mem_toFinset.mpr (Ne.symm h))

end DFinsupp

end

-- Author: @toskua, Avocado
module

public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.DFinsupp

/-!
# Dependent finitely supported functions with product fibers

For dependent module families `M N : ι → Type*`, a finitely supported
function with product-valued fibers is linearly equivalent to a pair of
finitely supported functions:

```text
(Π₀ i, M i × N i) ≃ₗ[R] (Π₀ i, M i) × (Π₀ i, N i).
```

The forward map applies the two projections with `DFinsupp.mapRange`.  The
inverse uses `DFinsupp.zipWith`; its finite-support witness is therefore built
from the union of the two input supports.  No decidable equality on the index
type is required by the equivalence itself.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false

universe uR uι uM uN

namespace DFinsupp

variable {R : Type uR} [Semiring R]
variable {ι : Type uι}
variable {M : ι → Type uM} {N : ι → Type uN}
variable [∀ i, AddCommMonoid (M i)] [∀ i, Module R (M i)]
variable [∀ i, AddCommMonoid (N i)] [∀ i, Module R (N i)]

/-- Split a dependent finitely supported function with product fibers into
the pair of its component families. -/
def prodLEquiv :
    (Π₀ i, M i × N i) ≃ₗ[R] (Π₀ i, M i) × (Π₀ i, N i) where
  toFun x :=
    (DFinsupp.mapRange (fun _ p => p.1) (fun _ => rfl) x,
      DFinsupp.mapRange (fun _ p => p.2) (fun _ => rfl) x)
  invFun x :=
    DFinsupp.zipWith (fun _ m n => (m, n)) (fun _ => rfl) x.1 x.2
  left_inv x := by
    ext i <;> rfl
  right_inv x := by
    apply Prod.ext <;> ext i <;> rfl
  map_add' x y := by
    apply Prod.ext <;> ext i <;> rfl
  map_smul' r x := by
    apply Prod.ext <;> ext i <;> rfl

/-- Coordinate formula for the first forward component. -/
@[simp]
theorem prodLEquiv_apply_fst_apply
    (x : Π₀ i, M i × N i) (i : ι) :
    (prodLEquiv (R := R) x).1 i = (x i).1 :=
  rfl

/-- Coordinate formula for the second forward component. -/
@[simp]
theorem prodLEquiv_apply_snd_apply
    (x : Π₀ i, M i × N i) (i : ι) :
    (prodLEquiv (R := R) x).2 i = (x i).2 :=
  rfl

/-- Coordinate formula for the inverse product assembly. -/
@[simp]
theorem prodLEquiv_symm_apply_apply
    (x : (Π₀ i, M i) × (Π₀ i, N i)) (i : ι) :
    ((prodLEquiv (R := R)).symm x) i = (x.1 i, x.2 i) :=
  rfl

/-- Splitting a one-coordinate vector splits its product-valued coordinate. -/
@[simp]
theorem prodLEquiv_single [DecidableEq ι]
    (i : ι) (x : M i × N i) :
    prodLEquiv (R := R) (DFinsupp.single i x) =
      (DFinsupp.single i x.1, DFinsupp.single i x.2) := by
  apply Prod.ext
  · exact DFinsupp.mapRange_single
      (f := fun i (p : M i × N i) => p.1) (hf := fun _ => rfl)
  · exact DFinsupp.mapRange_single
      (f := fun i (p : M i × N i) => p.2) (hf := fun _ => rfl)

/-- The inverse sends two one-coordinate vectors at the same index to the
corresponding product-valued one-coordinate vector. -/
@[simp]
theorem prodLEquiv_symm_single_single [DecidableEq ι]
    (i : ι) (m : M i) (n : N i) :
    (prodLEquiv (R := R)).symm
        (DFinsupp.single i m, DFinsupp.single i n) =
      DFinsupp.single i (m, n) := by
  exact DFinsupp.zipWith_single_single
    (fun _ m n => (m, n)) (fun _ => rfl) m n

end DFinsupp

end

module

public import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Group.Finset.Basic
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Determinant

/-!
# Determinants after basis-column normalization

This file records the determinant factorization obtained by extracting a
possibly different power of one scalar from every column of a linear
endomorphism.

## Main result

* `LinearMap.det_eq_pow_sum_mul_det_of_apply_basis`: if, on a finite basis
  `b`, two endomorphisms satisfy

  ```text
  f (b i) = π ^ c i • g (b i),
  ```

  then

  ```text
  det f = π ^ (∑ i, c i) * det g.
  ```
* `LinearMap.UniformizerColumnNormalization`: bundles the basis, extracted
  exponents, normalized endomorphism, and column identities; its `det_eq`
  theorem applies the factorization directly.

The statement is valid over an arbitrary commutative ring.  In particular,
`π` need not be regular or a uniformizer; those hypotheses belong only to
applications which construct `g` by dividing the columns of `f`.  The
explicit finite basis supplies the determinant data, so no separate
`Module.Free` or `Module.Finite` instance is required.

## Informal proof

Write both endomorphisms in the basis `b`.  The hypothesis says that column
`i` of the matrix of `f` is column `i` of the matrix of `g`, multiplied by
`π ^ c i`.  Hence

```text
matrix(f) = matrix(g) * diagonal(i ↦ π ^ c i).
```

Taking determinants turns the matrix product into a product.  The determinant
of the diagonal factor is `∏ i, π ^ c i`, and collecting powers of the common
base `π` changes this product to `π ^ ∑ i, c i`.
-/

@[expose] public section

noncomputable section

set_option autoImplicit false

open scoped BigOperators

universe uR uM uI

namespace LinearMap

variable {R : Type uR} {M : Type uM} {ι : Type uI}
variable [CommRing R] [Fintype ι]
variable [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]

/-- Extracting the power `π ^ c i` from basis column `i` extracts the sum of
the exponents from the determinant.

This is a columnwise factorization theorem, not a division theorem: the
normalized endomorphism `g` and the displayed basis equalities are supplied
as data.  Consequently no regularity assumption on `π` is required. -/
theorem det_eq_pow_sum_mul_det_of_apply_basis
    (b : Module.Basis ι R M) (π : R) (c : ι → ℕ)
    (f g : M →ₗ[R] M)
    (h : ∀ i, f (b i) = π ^ c i • g (b i)) :
    f.det = π ^ (∑ i, c i) * g.det := by
  classical
  have hmatrix :
      LinearMap.toMatrix b b f =
        LinearMap.toMatrix b b g * Matrix.diagonal (fun i ↦ π ^ c i) := by
    ext i j
    rw [LinearMap.toMatrix_apply, h j, map_smul, Matrix.mul_diagonal,
      LinearMap.toMatrix_apply, Finsupp.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, mul_comm]
  calc
    f.det = (LinearMap.toMatrix b b f).det :=
      (LinearMap.det_toMatrix b f).symm
    _ = (LinearMap.toMatrix b b g *
          Matrix.diagonal (fun i ↦ π ^ c i)).det := by rw [hmatrix]
    _ = (LinearMap.toMatrix b b g).det *
          (Matrix.diagonal (fun i ↦ π ^ c i)).det := by
      rw [Matrix.det_mul]
    _ = g.det * ∏ i, π ^ c i := by
      rw [LinearMap.det_toMatrix, Matrix.det_diagonal]
    _ = π ^ (∑ i, c i) * g.det := by
      rw [Finset.prod_pow_eq_pow_sum]
      exact mul_comm _ _

/-- Basis-indexed data exhibiting an endomorphism as columnwise powers of
one scalar times a normalized endomorphism. -/
structure UniformizerColumnNormalization {R : Type uR} {M : Type uM}
    [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (pi : R) (f : M →ₗ[R] M) where
  index : Type uI
  indexFintype : Fintype index
  basis : Module.Basis index R M
  exponent : index → ℕ
  normalized : M →ₗ[R] M
  apply_basis : ∀ i,
    f (basis i) = pi ^ exponent i • normalized (basis i)

namespace UniformizerColumnNormalization

variable {pi : R} {f : M →ₗ[R] M}

/-- Construct bundled column-normalization data from basiswise divisibility
witnesses.  The normalized endomorphism is the linear map sending each basis
vector to a chosen quotient column. -/
noncomputable def ofExists (b : Module.Basis ι R M) (pi : R)
    (c : ι → ℕ) (f : M →ₗ[R] M)
    (h : ∀ i, ∃ y : M, f (b i) = pi ^ c i • y) :
    UniformizerColumnNormalization pi f where
  index := ι
  indexFintype := inferInstance
  basis := b
  exponent := c
  normalized := b.constr R fun i ↦ Classical.choose (h i)
  apply_basis := fun i ↦ by
    rw [Module.Basis.constr_basis]
    exact Classical.choose_spec (h i)

/-- Total scalar exponent extracted from all basis columns. -/
noncomputable def totalExponent
    (D : UniformizerColumnNormalization pi f) : ℕ := by
  letI : Fintype D.index := D.indexFintype
  exact ∑ i, D.exponent i

@[simp]
theorem totalExponent_ofExists (b : Module.Basis ι R M) (pi : R)
    (c : ι → ℕ) (f : M →ₗ[R] M)
    (h : ∀ i, ∃ y : M, f (b i) = pi ^ c i • y) :
    (ofExists b pi c f h).totalExponent = ∑ i, c i :=
  rfl

/-- Determinant factorization supplied by bundled column-normalization
data. -/
theorem det_eq (D : UniformizerColumnNormalization pi f) :
    f.det = pi ^ D.totalExponent * D.normalized.det := by
  let _ : Fintype D.index := D.indexFintype
  exact det_eq_pow_sum_mul_det_of_apply_basis
    D.basis pi D.exponent f D.normalized D.apply_basis

end UniformizerColumnNormalization

end LinearMap

end

module

public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Determinant
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.Block

/-!
# Determinants of dependent componentwise endomorphisms

Mathlib's `LinearMap.det_pi` computes the determinant of a componentwise
endomorphism of `ι → M`, where every component is the same finite free
module.  This file proves the dependent-family version: the modules `M i`
may have different ranks.

## Informal proof

Choose a finite basis `b i` of each component `M i`.  The dependent Pi basis
`Pi.basis b` is indexed by the sigma type of all component basis indices.
In that basis the componentwise endomorphism has matrix

```text
Matrix.blockDiagonal' (fun i => matrix (f i)).
```

Indeed, a basis vector supported in component `j` stays in component `j`, so
every off-diagonal block is zero, while the `j`-th diagonal block is exactly
the matrix of `f j`.

For completeness, the required determinant formula for unequal block sizes
is proved first.  Give the finite outer index an arbitrary linear order and
view `blockDiagonal'` as block triangular.  The block-triangular determinant
theorem expresses its determinant as the product of its square diagonal
blocks.  The fiber of `Sigma.fst` over `i` is canonically equivalent to the
index type of the `i`-th block, so determinant invariance under reindexing
identifies that square block with the original matrix.  Applying this matrix
formula to the dependent Pi basis gives the result.

## Reconstructing a block-diagonal endomorphism

For an arbitrary endomorphism `F` of a finite dependent product, its `(i,j)`
block is the composite

```text
M j --single j--> (∀ i, M i) --F--> (∀ i, M i) --proj i--> M i.
```

Suppose every block with `i ≠ j` is zero.  Decompose an arbitrary vector as
the finite sum `∑ j, Pi.single j (x j)` and apply linearity of `F`.  After
evaluating at coordinate `i`, all terms except `j = i` vanish by the block
hypothesis.  The surviving term is the diagonal block applied to `x i`.
Function and linear-map extensionality therefore identify `F` with the
componentwise endomorphism assembled from its diagonal blocks.  This argument
uses neither matrices nor finite-free hypotheses.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
noncomputable section

open scoped BigOperators

universe uR uI uM uK

namespace Matrix

variable {R : Type uR} [CommRing R]
variable {ι : Type uI} [Fintype ι]
variable {κ : ι → Type uK} [∀ i, Fintype (κ i)]

/-- The index type of one block is equivalent to the corresponding fiber of
the sigma-type block projection. -/
private noncomputable def sigmaBlockFiberEquiv (i : ι) :
    κ i ≃ {x : Sigma κ // x.1 = i} :=
  Equiv.ofBijective
    (fun j => ⟨⟨i, j⟩, rfl⟩)
    ⟨fun _ _ h => sigma_mk_injective (congrArg Subtype.val h), fun x => by
      rcases x with ⟨⟨j, x⟩, hj⟩
      change j = i at hj
      subst j
      exact ⟨x, rfl⟩⟩

omit [Fintype ι] [∀ i, Fintype (κ i)] in
private theorem toSquareBlock_blockDiagonal'_eq_reindex
    [DecidableEq ι]
    (A : ∀ i, Matrix (κ i) (κ i) R) (i : ι) :
    (Matrix.blockDiagonal' A).toSquareBlock Sigma.fst i =
      Matrix.reindex (sigmaBlockFiberEquiv (κ := κ) i)
        (sigmaBlockFiberEquiv (κ := κ) i) (A i) := by
  ext ⟨⟨j, x⟩, hj⟩ ⟨⟨k, y⟩, hk⟩
  change j = i at hj
  change k = i at hk
  subst j
  subst k
  simp only [Matrix.toSquareBlock_def, Matrix.of_apply,
    Matrix.reindex_apply, Matrix.submatrix_apply,
    Matrix.blockDiagonal'_apply_eq]
  let e := sigmaBlockFiberEquiv (κ := κ) i
  change A i x y =
    A i (e.symm ⟨⟨i, x⟩, rfl⟩) (e.symm ⟨⟨i, y⟩, rfl⟩)
  have hx : e.symm ⟨⟨i, x⟩, rfl⟩ = x := by
    apply e.symm_apply_eq.mpr
    apply Subtype.ext
    rfl
  have hy : e.symm ⟨⟨i, y⟩, rfl⟩ = y := by
    apply e.symm_apply_eq.mpr
    apply Subtype.ext
    rfl
  rw [hx, hy]

private theorem det_blockDiagonal'_of_linearOrder
    [DecidableEq ι] [∀ i, DecidableEq (κ i)] [LinearOrder ι]
    (A : ∀ i, Matrix (κ i) (κ i) R) :
    (Matrix.blockDiagonal' A).det = ∏ i, (A i).det := by
  rw [(Matrix.blockTriangular_blockDiagonal' A).det_fintype]
  apply Finset.prod_congr rfl
  intro i _
  rw [toSquareBlock_blockDiagonal'_eq_reindex,
    Matrix.det_reindex_self]

/-- The determinant of a finite dependent block-diagonal matrix is the
product of the determinants of its blocks. -/
theorem det_blockDiagonal' [DecidableEq ι] [∀ i, DecidableEq (κ i)]
    (A : ∀ i, Matrix (κ i) (κ i) R) :
    (Matrix.blockDiagonal' A).det = ∏ i, (A i).det := by
  classical
  let horder : LinearOrder ι := linearOrderOfSTO WellOrderingRel
  exact @det_blockDiagonal'_of_linearOrder R _ ι _ κ _ _ _ horder A

end Matrix

namespace LinearMap

variable {R : Type uR} [CommRing R]
variable {ι : Type uI}
variable {M : ι → Type uM}
variable [∀ i, AddCommGroup (M i)] [∀ i, Module R (M i)]

/-- The `(i,j)` block of an endomorphism of a dependent product: include the
`j`-th component, apply the endomorphism, then project to component `i`. -/
noncomputable def dependentPiBlock
    (F : (∀ i, M i) →ₗ[R] ∀ i, M i) (i j : ι) : M j →ₗ[R] M i := by
  classical
  exact (LinearMap.proj i).comp (F.comp (LinearMap.single R M j))

/-- A finite dependent-product endomorphism with zero off-diagonal blocks is
the componentwise endomorphism assembled from its diagonal blocks. -/
theorem eq_pi_diagonal_of_dependentPiBlock_eq_zero
    [Finite ι]
    (F : (∀ i, M i) →ₗ[R] ∀ i, M i)
    (hF : ∀ i j : ι, i ≠ j → dependentPiBlock F i j = 0) :
    F = LinearMap.pi fun i => (dependentPiBlock F i i).comp (LinearMap.proj i) := by
  classical
  let _ : Fintype ι := Fintype.ofFinite ι
  apply LinearMap.ext
  intro x
  funext i
  change F x i = dependentPiBlock F i i (x i)
  calc
    F x i = F (∑ j, Pi.single j (x j)) i := by
      rw [LinearMap.sum_single_apply]
    _ = ∑ j, F (Pi.single j (x j)) i := by
      rw [map_sum, Finset.sum_apply]
    _ = dependentPiBlock F i i (x i) := by
      change (∑ j, dependentPiBlock F i j (x j)) = dependentPiBlock F i i (x i)
      rw [Finset.sum_eq_single i]
      · intro j _ hji
        rw [hF i j hji.symm, LinearMap.zero_apply]
      · simp

variable [Fintype ι]
variable [∀ i, Module.Free R (M i)] [∀ i, Module.Finite R (M i)]

/-- Determinant of a componentwise endomorphism of a finite dependent
product.  Unlike `LinearMap.det_pi`, the component modules may have unequal
ranks. -/
theorem det_pi_dependent (f : ∀ i, M i →ₗ[R] M i) :
    (LinearMap.pi (fun i => (f i).comp (LinearMap.proj i))).det =
      ∏ i, (f i).det := by
  classical
  let b := fun i => Module.Free.chooseBasis R (M i)
  let B := Pi.basis b
  simp_rw [← LinearMap.det_toMatrix B, ← LinearMap.det_toMatrix (b _)]
  have hmatrix :
      LinearMap.toMatrix B B
          (LinearMap.pi fun i => (f i).comp (LinearMap.proj i)) =
        Matrix.blockDiagonal'
          (fun i => LinearMap.toMatrix (b i) (b i) (f i)) := by
    ext ⟨i, x⟩ ⟨j, y⟩
    simp only [LinearMap.toMatrix_apply', B, Pi.basis_apply, Pi.basis_repr,
      LinearMap.pi_apply, LinearMap.coe_comp, Function.comp_apply,
      LinearMap.coe_proj, Function.eval,
      Matrix.blockDiagonal'_apply]
    split_ifs with h
    · subst j
      simp
    · simp [h]
  rw [hmatrix, Matrix.det_blockDiagonal']

end LinearMap

namespace LinearEquiv

variable {R : Type uR} [CommRing R]
variable {ι : Type uI} [Fintype ι]
variable {M : ι → Type uM}
variable [∀ i, AddCommGroup (M i)] [∀ i, Module R (M i)]
variable [∀ i, Module.Free R (M i)] [∀ i, Module.Finite R (M i)]

/-- The determinant of a dependent product of linear equivalences is the
product of their determinants. -/
theorem det_piCongrRight (f : ∀ i, M i ≃ₗ[R] M i) :
    LinearEquiv.det (LinearEquiv.piCongrRight f) =
      ∏ i, LinearEquiv.det (f i) := by
  apply Units.ext
  rw [LinearEquiv.coe_det, Units.coe_prod]
  have hmap : (LinearEquiv.piCongrRight f).toLinearMap =
      LinearMap.pi (fun i => (f i).toLinearMap.comp
        (LinearMap.proj i)) := by
    apply LinearMap.ext
    intro x
    funext i
    rfl
  rw [hmap, LinearMap.det_pi_dependent]
  simp only [LinearEquiv.coe_det]

end LinearEquiv

end

-- Author: @toskua, Avocado
module

public import MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.Basis.FiniteFiltration
public import MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.Determinant.FiniteFiltration

/-!
# Determinants of filtration-unipotent endomorphisms

Let

```text
F 0 ≤ F 1 ≤ ... ≤ F n = M
```

be a finite filtration from zero to the whole module.  Choose a basis of
every successive quotient and assemble them into
`Module.Basis.ofFiltration`.  This file proves that an endomorphism has
determinant one if it fixes every assembled graded basis vector modulo the
preceding stage.

More precisely, write `B` for the assembled basis and suppose

```text
U (B ⟨i,a⟩) - B ⟨i,a⟩ ∈ F i
```

for every grade `i` and graded basis index `a`.  Then `U.det = 1`.

## Informal proof

### Prefix agreement

For `j ≤ n`, an index `i : Fin j` also defines an index of the final
assembled basis.  Repeated use of `Module.Basis.ofFiltrationStage_castSucc`
shows that the `i`-th vector of the stage-`j` basis and the corresponding
ambient vector have the same underlying element of `M`.  The proof is by
induction on the final cutoff.  At a successor cutoff, either `j` is already
below the previous cutoff, in which case apply the induction hypothesis and
one cast-successor identity, or `j` is the new final cutoff, in which case
the statement is reflexive.

### Derived stage stability

Fix `j ≤ n` and expand `x : F j` in the explicit basis
`ofFiltrationStage ... j`.  For a basis vector introduced in grade `i < j`,
prefix agreement identifies its ambient value with `B ⟨i,a⟩`.  The
hypothesis places its error under `U` in `F i`, hence in `F j`; the vector
itself already belongs to `F j`.  Thus its image under `U` belongs to `F j`.
Linearity and the finite basis expansion prove `F j ≤ (F j).comap U`.

### Adjacent quotients

Restrict `U` to every stable stage.  For adjacent stages, identify `F i`
with its copy inside `F (i+1)` by
`Submodule.comapSubtypeEquivOfLe`.  The restricted maps intertwine on
underlying values, producing a `LinearMap.InvariantExtension`.

The quotient basis vector `b i a` is represented by
`Module.Basis.ofFiltrationStageVector ... i a`.  Its ambient value is exactly
the assembled grade-`i` basis vector.  The error hypothesis therefore says
that the induced quotient map fixes this representative modulo `F i`.
Basis extensionality proves that every successive quotient map is
`LinearMap.id`; its determinant is one.

### Determinant product

The explicit stage bases and quotient bases install finite-free structures
on all modules used by
`LinearMap.det_eq_prod_graded_of_bottom_subsingleton`.  The bottom equality
`F 0 = ⊥` makes the first stage subsingleton.  The determinant product is
therefore a product of ones.  Finally, the canonical equivalence `F n ≃ M`
conjugates the last restricted endomorphism to `U`, so determinant invariance
under conjugacy gives `U.det = 1`.

The proof includes `n = 0`: then the bottom is also the top, so the ambient
module is subsingleton and the empty determinant product is one.  Empty
graded index types are harmless.  No field hypothesis is used.

## API novelty

The closest existing APIs are:

* `Module.Basis.ofFiltrationStage_castSucc` and
  `Module.Basis.ofFiltrationStageVector_mk`, which provide the exact basis
  representatives but do not prove stability of an arbitrary endomorphism;
* `LinearMap.det_eq_prod_graded_of_bottom_subsingleton`, which factors a
  determinant once invariant stages and quotient maps are already supplied;
* matrix triangular determinant lemmas, which would require an additional
  order on the dependent basis index and would duplicate the filtration
  infrastructure.

The theorem below is therefore the missing bridge: it derives both stage
stability and graded identity from the basis-level error hypothesis.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
noncomputable section

open Module
open scoped BigOperators

universe uR uM uι

namespace Module.Basis

variable {R : Type uR} {M : Type uM} [CommRing R]
variable [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
variable {κ : ℕ → Type uι}

/-- Passing an early filtration basis vector through any number of later
stages does not change its underlying ambient value. -/
private theorem coe_ofFiltrationStage_eq_of_le
    (F : ℕ → Submodule R M) (hzero : F 0 = ⊥)
    (n : ℕ)
    (hF : ∀ i : Fin n, F i.val ≤ F (i.val + 1))
    (b : ∀ i : Fin n,
      Basis (κ i.val) R
        (F (i.val + 1) ⧸ (F i.val).comap (F (i.val + 1)).subtype))
    {j : ℕ} (hj : j ≤ n) (i : Fin j) (a : κ i.val) :
    ((ofFiltrationStage F hzero κ j
        (fun k => hF (k.castLE hj))
        (fun k => b (k.castLE hj)) ⟨i, a⟩ : F j) : M) =
      ((ofFiltrationStage F hzero κ n hF b
        ⟨i.castLE hj, a⟩ : F n) : M) := by
  induction n with
  | zero => exact Fin.elim0 (i.castLE hj)
  | succ n ih =>
      by_cases hjn : j ≤ n
      · calc
          _ = ((ofFiltrationStage F hzero κ n
                (fun k => hF k.castSucc)
                (fun k => b k.castSucc)
                ⟨i.castLE hjn, a⟩ : F n) : M) :=
            ih (fun k => hF k.castSucc) (fun k => b k.castSucc) hjn
          _ = ((ofFiltrationStage F hzero κ (n + 1) hF b
                ⟨i.castLE hj, a⟩ : F (n + 1)) : M) := by
            symm
            simpa using ofFiltrationStage_castSucc F hzero κ n hF b
              (i.castLE hjn) a
      · have hjeq : j = n + 1 := by omega
        subst j
        rfl

private theorem filtration_mono_of_succ
    (F : ℕ → Submodule R M) (n : ℕ)
    (hF : ∀ i : Fin n, F i.val ≤ F (i.val + 1))
    {i j : ℕ} (hij : i ≤ j) (hj : j ≤ n) : F i ≤ F j := by
  revert hj
  refine Nat.le_induction (m := i)
    (P := fun j _ => j ≤ n → F i ≤ F j) ?_ ?_ j hij
  · intro _
    exact le_rfl
  · intro k hik ih hk1n
    exact (ih (Nat.le_trans (Nat.le_succ k) hk1n)).trans
      (hF ⟨k, Nat.lt_of_succ_le hk1n⟩)

/-- A vector in a prefix filtration basis agrees in `M` with the
corresponding vector of the final assembled basis. -/
theorem ofFiltration_apply_eq_ofFiltrationStage
    (F : ℕ → Submodule R M) (hzero : F 0 = ⊥)
    (n : ℕ)
    (hF : ∀ i : Fin n, F i.val ≤ F (i.val + 1))
    (b : ∀ i : Fin n,
      Basis (κ i.val) R
        (F (i.val + 1) ⧸ (F i.val).comap (F (i.val + 1)).subtype))
    (htop : F n = ⊤)
    {j : ℕ} (hj : j ≤ n) (i : Fin j) (a : κ i.val) :
    ofFiltration F hzero κ n hF b htop ⟨i.castLE hj, a⟩ =
      ((ofFiltrationStage F hzero κ j
        (fun k => hF (k.castLE hj))
        (fun k => b (k.castLE hj)) ⟨i, a⟩ : F j) : M) := by
  rw [ofFiltration_apply]
  exact (coe_ofFiltrationStage_eq_of_le F hzero n hF b hj i a).symm

/-- The basis-level condition `U b - b ∈ F i` on every vector introduced at
grade `i` forces every filtration stage to be `U`-stable. -/
theorem ofFiltration_stable
    (F : ℕ → Submodule R M) (hzero : F 0 = ⊥)
    (n : ℕ)
    (hF : ∀ i : Fin n, F i.val ≤ F (i.val + 1))
    (b : ∀ i : Fin n,
      Basis (κ i.val) R
        (F (i.val + 1) ⧸ (F i.val).comap (F (i.val + 1)).subtype))
    (htop : F n = ⊤)
    (U : M →ₗ[R] M)
    (hU : ∀ i : Fin n, ∀ a : κ i.val,
      U (ofFiltration F hzero κ n hF b htop ⟨i, a⟩) -
          ofFiltration F hzero κ n hF b htop ⟨i, a⟩ ∈ F i.val)
    [∀ i : Fin n, Finite (κ i.val)]
    (j : ℕ) (hj : j ≤ n) : F j ≤ (F j).comap U := by
  let _ : ∀ i : Fin n, Fintype (κ i.val) := fun _ => Fintype.ofFinite _
  let _ : ∀ i : Fin j, Fintype (κ i.val) := fun i =>
    inferInstanceAs (Fintype (κ (i.castLE hj).val))
  let bj := ofFiltrationStage F hzero κ j
    (fun k => hF (k.castLE hj)) (fun k => b (k.castLE hj))
  intro x hx
  let xj : F j := ⟨x, hx⟩
  have hsum := bj.sum_repr xj
  have hsumM := congrArg (fun z : F j => (z : M)) hsum
  have hcoe :
      (((∑ p, (bj.repr xj) p • bj p : F j) : F j) : M) =
        ∑ p, (bj.repr xj) p • (bj p : M) := by
    change (F j).subtype (∑ p, (bj.repr xj) p • bj p) = _
    rw [map_sum]
    simp only [map_smul]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro p _
    rfl
  have hsumM' :
      (∑ p, (bj.repr xj) p • (bj p : M)) = (xj : M) :=
    hcoe.symm.trans hsumM
  change U (xj : M) ∈ F j
  rw [← hsumM', map_sum]
  exact Submodule.sum_mem _ fun p _ => by
    rw [map_smul]
    apply Submodule.smul_mem
    have hpref := ofFiltration_apply_eq_ofFiltrationStage
      F hzero n hF b htop hj p.1 p.2
    have herr := hU (p.1.castLE hj) p.2
    rw [hpref] at herr
    have herrj : U (bj p : M) - (bj p : M) ∈ F j :=
      filtration_mono_of_succ F n hF (Nat.le_of_lt p.1.isLt) hj herr
    rw [← sub_add_cancel (U (bj p : M)) (bj p : M)]
    exact Submodule.add_mem _ herrj (bj p).property

end Module.Basis

namespace LinearMap

open Module.Basis

variable {R : Type uR} {M : Type uM} [CommRing R]
variable [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
variable {κ : ℕ → Type uι}

/-- An endomorphism that fixes each assembled filtration-basis vector modulo
the preceding filtration stage has determinant one.  Stage stability and
identity on the successive quotients are conclusions of the proof, not
inputs. -/
theorem det_eq_one_of_sub_mem_ofFiltration
    (F : ℕ → Submodule R M) (hzero : F 0 = ⊥)
    (n : ℕ)
    (hF : ∀ i : Fin n, F i.val ≤ F (i.val + 1))
    (b : ∀ i : Fin n,
      Basis (κ i.val) R
        (F (i.val + 1) ⧸ (F i.val).comap (F (i.val + 1)).subtype))
    (htop : F n = ⊤)
    (U : M →ₗ[R] M)
    (hU : ∀ i : Fin n, ∀ a : κ i.val,
      U (ofFiltration F hzero κ n hF b htop ⟨i, a⟩) -
          ofFiltration F hzero κ n hF b htop ⟨i, a⟩ ∈ F i.val)
    [∀ i : Fin n, Finite (κ i.val)] :
    U.det = 1 := by
  let _ : ∀ i : Fin n, Fintype (κ i.val) := fun _ => Fintype.ofFinite _
  let B := ofFiltration F hzero κ n hF b htop
  let _ : Module.Free R M := Module.Free.of_basis B
  let _ : Module.Finite R M := Module.Finite.of_basis B
  let stageLE : ∀ j : Fin (n + 1), j.val ≤ n := fun j =>
    Nat.lt_succ_iff.mp j.isLt
  let stageBasis (j : Fin (n + 1)) :
      Basis (FiltrationIndex κ j.val) R (F j.val) :=
    ofFiltrationStage F hzero κ j.val
      (fun k => hF (k.castLE (stageLE j)))
      (fun k => b (k.castLE (stageLE j)))
  let _ : ∀ j : Fin (n + 1), Fintype (FiltrationIndex κ j.val) := fun j => by
    let _ : ∀ i : Fin j.val, Fintype (κ i.val) := fun i =>
      inferInstanceAs (Fintype (κ (i.castLE (stageLE j)).val))
    infer_instance
  let _ : ∀ j : Fin (n + 1), Module.Free R (F j.val) := fun j =>
    Module.Free.of_basis (stageBasis j)
  let _ : ∀ j : Fin (n + 1), Module.Finite R (F j.val) := fun j =>
    Module.Finite.of_basis (stageBasis j)
  let stable (j : Fin (n + 1)) : F j.val ≤ (F j.val).comap U :=
    ofFiltration_stable F hzero n hF b htop U hU j.val (stageLE j)
  let endomorphism (j : Fin (n + 1)) : F j.val →ₗ[R] F j.val :=
    U.restrict (stable j)
  let step (i : Fin n) :
      InvariantExtension (endomorphism i.castSucc) (endomorphism i.succ) :=
    { submodule := (F i.val).comap (F (i.val + 1)).subtype
      stable := by
        intro x hx
        change U (x : M) ∈ F i.val
        exact stable i.castSucc hx
      equiv := (Submodule.comapSubtypeEquivOfLe (hF i)).symm
      intertwines := by
        apply LinearMap.ext
        intro x
        rfl }
  have hquotient (i : Fin n) :
      (step i).quotientMap = LinearMap.id := by
    apply (b i).ext
    intro a
    rw [← ofFiltrationStageVector_mk F hzero κ n hF b i a]
    rw [InvariantExtension.quotientMap_mk]
    apply (Submodule.Quotient.eq _).mpr
    change U
        ((ofFiltrationStageVector F hzero κ n hF b i a : F (i.val + 1)) : M) -
      ((ofFiltrationStageVector F hzero κ n hF b i a : F (i.val + 1)) : M) ∈
        F i.val
    simpa only [ofFiltrationStageVector, ofFiltration_apply] using hU i a
  let _ : Subsingleton (F (0 : Fin (n + 1)).val) := by
    change Subsingleton (F 0)
    rw [hzero]
    infer_instance
  have hdetStage : (endomorphism (Fin.last n)).det = 1 := by
    rw [det_eq_prod_graded_of_bottom_subsingleton
      endomorphism step (fun i => Module.Free.of_basis (b i))]
    simp only [hquotient, LinearMap.det_id, Finset.prod_const_one]
  let eTop : F n ≃ₗ[R] M :=
    (LinearEquiv.ofEq (F n) ⊤ htop).trans Submodule.topEquiv
  have hconj : eTop.conj (endomorphism (Fin.last n)) = U := by
    apply LinearMap.ext
    intro x
    obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := eTop.surjective x
    rfl
  calc
    U.det = (eTop.conj (endomorphism (Fin.last n))).det := by rw [hconj]
    _ = (endomorphism (Fin.last n)).det := by
      change LinearMap.det
          (((eTop : F n →ₗ[R] M) ∘ₗ endomorphism (Fin.last n)) ∘ₗ
            (eTop.symm : M →ₗ[R] F n)) =
        LinearMap.det (endomorphism (Fin.last n))
      exact LinearMap.det_conj (endomorphism (Fin.last n)) eTop
    _ = 1 := hdetStage

end LinearMap

end

module

public import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Fin
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Determinant

/-!
# Determinants along finite invariant filtrations

This file packages and iterates the determinant factorization for an
endomorphism preserving a submodule.  It is intended for finite filtrations
whose stages and successive quotients are finite free modules.

## Main declarations

* `LinearMap.InvariantExtension` records one inclusion of a filtration stage
  as an invariant submodule of the next stage.
* `LinearMap.InvariantExtension.quotientMap` is the induced endomorphism on
  the successive quotient.
* `LinearMap.InvariantExtension.det_eq_det_mul_det_quotientMap` is the
  one-step determinant factorization.
* `LinearMap.det_eq_det_mul_prod_graded` iterates the factorization through a
  finite tower.
* `LinearMap.det_eq_prod_graded_of_bottom_subsingleton` removes the bottom
  determinant when the initial stage is zero.

## Informal proof

For one step, let `f` act on the lower stage `V`, let `g` act on the next
stage `W`, and identify `V` with a `g`-invariant submodule `S` of `W`.
Mathlib's `LinearMap.det_eq_det_mul_det` chooses a basis of `S`, extends it by
a basis of `W/S`, and writes the matrix of `g` in block upper-triangular
form.  It gives

`det(g) = det(g|S) * det(g on W/S)`.

The stored intertwining equality says that `g|S` is conjugate to `f` through
the identification `V ~= S`.  Determinants are invariant under conjugation,
so the first factor is `det(f)`.

For a finite tower, apply this one-step identity at every adjacent pair.  A
plain induction over `Fin n` multiplies the successive quotient determinants:
if `d_(i+1) = d_i * q_i`, then

`d_n = d_0 * product_i q_i`.

When the bottom stage is a zero module, its determinant is one, leaving only
the product over the graded quotients.

The freeness of every successive quotient is explicit.  Over an arbitrary
commutative ring it does not follow merely from freeness of the two adjacent
stages; this hypothesis is therefore not hidden or weakened.
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped BigOperators

universe u v w

namespace LinearMap

variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
variable {V : Type v} {W : Type w}
variable [AddCommGroup V] [Module R V]
variable [AddCommGroup W] [Module R W]

/-- One step of an invariant filtration.

The lower endomorphism `f` is identified with the restriction of the upper
endomorphism `g` to `submodule`.  The quotient endomorphism is consequently
the action of `g` on the corresponding successive graded piece. -/
structure InvariantExtension (f : V →ₗ[R] V) (g : W →ₗ[R] W) where
  /-- The lower filtration stage inside the next stage. -/
  submodule : Submodule R W
  /-- The next-stage endomorphism preserves the lower stage. -/
  stable : submodule ≤ submodule.comap g
  /-- Identification of the abstract lower stage with the invariant
  submodule. -/
  equiv : V ≃ₗ[R] submodule
  /-- Under `equiv`, the lower endomorphism intertwines with the restriction
  of the upper endomorphism. -/
  intertwines :
    (equiv : V →ₗ[R] submodule) ∘ₗ f =
      (g.restrict stable) ∘ₗ (equiv : V →ₗ[R] submodule)

namespace InvariantExtension

variable {f : V →ₗ[R] V} {g : W →ₗ[R] W}

/-- The intertwining square in an invariant extension, rewritten as a
conjugation identity. -/
theorem conjugate_eq (E : InvariantExtension f g) :
    (E.equiv : V →ₗ[R] E.submodule) ∘ₗ f ∘ₗ
        (E.equiv.symm : E.submodule →ₗ[R] V) =
      g.restrict E.stable := by
  apply LinearMap.ext
  intro x
  have h := LinearMap.congr_fun E.intertwines (E.equiv.symm x)
  simpa using h

/-- The endomorphism induced on the successive quotient of an invariant
extension. -/
def quotientMap (E : InvariantExtension f g) :
    (W ⧸ E.submodule) →ₗ[R] (W ⧸ E.submodule) :=
  E.submodule.mapQ E.submodule g E.stable

/-- The quotient endomorphism sends the class of a representative to the
class of its image under the upper-stage endomorphism. -/
@[simp]
theorem quotientMap_mk (E : InvariantExtension f g) (x : W) :
    E.quotientMap (Submodule.Quotient.mk x : W ⧸ E.submodule) =
      (Submodule.Quotient.mk (g x) : W ⧸ E.submodule) := by
  simpa only [quotientMap] using
    (Submodule.mapQ_apply E.submodule E.submodule g (h := E.stable) x)

/-- Determinant factorization for one invariant extension.

This is the reusable one-step block-triangular formula.  The lower stage and
the quotient are required to be finite free in exactly the places needed by
`LinearMap.det_eq_det_mul_det`. -/
theorem det_eq_det_mul_det_quotientMap (E : InvariantExtension f g)
    [Module.Free R V] [Module.Finite R V] [Module.Finite R W]
    [Module.Free R (W ⧸ E.submodule)] :
    g.det = f.det * E.quotientMap.det := by
  let _ : Module.Free R E.submodule := Module.Free.of_equiv E.equiv
  let _ : Module.Finite R E.submodule := Module.Finite.equiv E.equiv
  calc
    g.det = (g.restrict E.stable).det * E.quotientMap.det :=
      g.det_eq_det_mul_det E.submodule E.stable
    _ = f.det * E.quotientMap.det := by
      rw [← E.conjugate_eq, LinearMap.det_conj]

end InvariantExtension

private theorem last_eq_first_mul_prod {n : ℕ} (d : Fin (n + 1) → R)
    (q : Fin n → R) (h : ∀ i, d i.succ = d i.castSucc * q i) :
    d (Fin.last n) = d 0 * ∏ i, q i := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp
  | succ n ih =>
      have hprefix :
          d (Fin.castSucc (Fin.last n)) =
            d 0 * ∏ i : Fin n, q i.castSucc := by
        apply ih (d := fun i ↦ d i.castSucc) (q := fun i ↦ q i.castSucc)
        intro i
        simpa using h i.castSucc
      calc
        d (Fin.last (n + 1)) =
            d (Fin.castSucc (Fin.last n)) * q (Fin.last n) := by
          simpa using h (Fin.last n)
        _ = (d 0 * ∏ i : Fin n, q i.castSucc) * q (Fin.last n) := by
          rw [hprefix]
        _ = d 0 * ((∏ i : Fin n, q i.castSucc) * q (Fin.last n)) := by
          rw [mul_assoc]
        _ = d 0 * ∏ i, q i := by
          rw [Fin.prod_univ_castSucc]

section FiniteTower

variable {n : ℕ} {M : Fin (n + 1) → Type v}
variable [∀ i, AddCommGroup (M i)] [∀ i, Module R (M i)]
variable [∀ i, Module.Free R (M i)] [∀ i, Module.Finite R (M i)]

/-- The determinant on the final stage of a finite invariant filtration is
the determinant on the initial stage times the product of the determinants
on all successive graded quotients.

The stages may be presented as different module types.  Each `step i`
identifies stage `i` with an invariant submodule of stage `i+1`; this avoids
choosing coercion-heavy nested subtypes and makes the theorem convenient for
filtrations transported through canonical linear equivalences. -/
theorem det_eq_det_mul_prod_graded (endomorphism : ∀ i, M i →ₗ[R] M i)
    (step : ∀ i : Fin n,
      InvariantExtension (endomorphism i.castSucc) (endomorphism i.succ))
    (quotientFree : ∀ i, Module.Free R (M i.succ ⧸ (step i).submodule)) :
    (endomorphism (Fin.last n)).det =
      (endomorphism 0).det * ∏ i, (step i).quotientMap.det := by
  refine last_eq_first_mul_prod
    (d := fun i ↦ (endomorphism i).det)
    (q := fun i ↦ (step i).quotientMap.det) ?_
  intro i
  let _ : Module.Free R (M i.succ ⧸ (step i).submodule) := quotientFree i
  exact (step i).det_eq_det_mul_det_quotientMap

/-- Version of `LinearMap.det_eq_det_mul_prod_graded` for a filtration whose
bottom determinant has already been identified with one. -/
theorem det_eq_prod_graded_of_bottom_det_eq_one
    (endomorphism : ∀ i, M i →ₗ[R] M i)
    (step : ∀ i : Fin n,
      InvariantExtension (endomorphism i.castSucc) (endomorphism i.succ))
    (quotientFree : ∀ i, Module.Free R (M i.succ ⧸ (step i).submodule))
    (hbottom : (endomorphism 0).det = 1) :
    (endomorphism (Fin.last n)).det = ∏ i, (step i).quotientMap.det := by
  rw [det_eq_det_mul_prod_graded endomorphism step quotientFree, hbottom, one_mul]

/-- Determinant product formula for a finite invariant filtration starting
at a zero module. -/
theorem det_eq_prod_graded_of_bottom_subsingleton
    (endomorphism : ∀ i, M i →ₗ[R] M i)
    (step : ∀ i : Fin n,
      InvariantExtension (endomorphism i.castSucc) (endomorphism i.succ))
    (quotientFree : ∀ i, Module.Free R (M i.succ ⧸ (step i).submodule))
    [Subsingleton (M 0)] :
    (endomorphism (Fin.last n)).det = ∏ i, (step i).quotientMap.det :=
  det_eq_prod_graded_of_bottom_det_eq_one endomorphism step quotientFree
    (LinearMap.det_eq_one_of_subsingleton _)

end FiniteTower

end LinearMap

module

public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Determinant
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Basis.Defs

/-!
# Determinants after transporting scalar coefficients

Let `e : R ≃+* S`, and let the same additive group `M` carry compatible
`R`- and `S`-module structures.  Compatibility means

```text
e c • x = c • x.
```

Suppose `fR : M →ₗ[R] M` and `fS : M →ₗ[S] M` have the same underlying
function.  Given a finite `R`-basis of `M`, this file proves

```text
e fR.det = fS.det.
```

## Informal proof

Let `b : Basis ι R M`, and use `b.mapCoeffs e h` as the corresponding
`S`-basis.  The transported basis has the same vectors as `b`.  Moreover,
`Module.Basis.mapCoeffs_repr` identifies the entire representation
equivalence. In particular, the `i`-th coordinate of any
vector in the transported basis is obtained by applying `e` to its `i`-th
coordinate in `b`.

Consequently, for every pair of basis indices `i,j`,

```text
toMatrix (b.mapCoeffs e h) (b.mapCoeffs e h) fS i j
  = e (toMatrix b b fR i j).
```

Indeed, both entries are the corresponding coordinate of the common value
`fS (b j) = fR (b j)`.  Matrix extensionality therefore identifies the
`S`-matrix with `Matrix.map e` of the `R`-matrix.

Now rewrite both linear-map determinants using `LinearMap.det_toMatrix`.
The matrix equality and `RingEquiv.map_det` give

```text
e (det (toMatrix b b fR))
  = det (toMatrix (b.mapCoeffs e h) (b.mapCoeffs e h) fS),
```

which is the desired equality.

The argument uses only commutative rings.  Empty finite bases are included:
both matrix determinants are the empty determinant `1`, and the same proof
applies unchanged.

## API novelty

The closest standard result is `Algebra.norm_eq_of_ringEquiv`, but that
compares determinants only for multiplication endomorphisms in algebra
norms.  It does not apply to arbitrary linear endomorphisms.  The ingredients
used here—`Basis.mapCoeffs_repr`, `RingEquiv.map_det`, and
`LinearMap.det_toMatrix`—do not already package this general transport law.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
noncomputable section

open Module

universe uR uS uM uι

namespace LinearMap

variable {R : Type uR} {S : Type uS} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
variable {M : Type uM} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module S M]
variable {ι : Type uι} [Finite ι]

/-- Determinants commute with transport along a scalar-ring equivalence when
the scalar actions and the underlying endomorphism agree. -/
theorem det_mapCoeffs (e : R ≃+* S)
    (h : ∀ (c : R) (x : M), e c • x = c • x)
    (b : Basis ι R M) (fR : M →ₗ[R] M) (fS : M →ₗ[S] M)
    (hf : ∀ x, fS x = fR x) :
    e fR.det = fS.det := by
  let _ : Fintype ι := Fintype.ofFinite ι
  classical
  have hmatrix :
      LinearMap.toMatrix (b.mapCoeffs e h) (b.mapCoeffs e h) fS =
        (LinearMap.toMatrix b b fR).map e := by
    ext i j
    rw [LinearMap.toMatrix_apply, Matrix.map_apply,
      Basis.mapCoeffs_apply, Basis.mapCoeffs_repr,
      LinearMap.toMatrix_apply]
    change e (b.repr (fS (b j)) i) = e (b.repr (fR (b j)) i)
    rw [hf]
  calc
    e fR.det = e (LinearMap.toMatrix b b fR).det := by
      rw [LinearMap.det_toMatrix]
    _ = ((LinearMap.toMatrix b b fR).map e).det := e.map_det _
    _ = (LinearMap.toMatrix (b.mapCoeffs e h)
        (b.mapCoeffs e h) fS).det := by rw [hmatrix]
    _ = fS.det := LinearMap.det_toMatrix _ _

end LinearMap

end

module

public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Charpoly.BaseChange
public import Mathlib.RingTheory.LocalRing.ResidueField.Basic
public import Mathlib.RingTheory.TensorProduct.Quotient

/-!
# Linear endomorphisms after quotient base change

Let `S` be a finite free algebra over a commutative ring `R`, let `I` be an
ideal of `R`, and let `f : S →ₗ[R] S`.  This file transports the ordinary
scalar extension of `f` across the canonical algebra equivalence

```text
S / I S  ≃  (R / I) ⊗[R] S.
```

The resulting endomorphism `f.quotientBaseChange I` sends the class
of `x` to the class of `f x`, and its determinant is the reduction of
`det f` modulo `I`.

For a local base ring, bijectivity of the residue endomorphism therefore
shows that `det f` is a unit.  The bundled determinant unit has residue equal
to the determinant unit of the induced residue equivalence.

## Main declarations

* `LinearMap.quotientBaseChange`: quotient-valued scalar extension of an
  arbitrary finite-free algebra endomorphism.
* `LinearMap.quotientBaseChange_mk`: representative formula.
* `LinearMap.det_quotientBaseChange`: determinant commutes with reduction.
* `LinearMap.isUnit_det_of_bijective_quotientBaseChange`: local unit
  detection from a bijective residue map.
* `LinearMap.detUnitOfBijectiveQuotientBaseChange`: the resulting determinant
  unit, with its value and residue formulas.

## Informal proof

The canonical equivalence
`Algebra.TensorProduct.quotIdealMapEquivQuotTensor S I` sends the class of
`x : S` to `1 ⊗ x`.  Conjugate the scalar extension
`f.baseChange (R / I)` by the inverse of this equivalence.  Since scalar
extension sends `1 ⊗ x` to `1 ⊗ f x`, conjugation gives the representative
formula.

Determinants are invariant under conjugation, and
`LinearMap.det_baseChange` identifies the determinant of the scalar extension
with `Ideal.Quotient.mk I (det f)`.  This proves determinant reduction without
choosing a basis of either quotient presentation.

Now suppose `R` is local and use its maximal ideal.  If the quotient map is
bijective, it is a linear equivalence, so its determinant is a unit and in
particular is nonzero in the residue field.  Determinant reduction says that
this nonzero element is the residue of `det f`.  An element of a local ring
has nonzero residue exactly when it is a unit.  Bundling that unit and applying
the same determinant equality proves the final residue formula.
-/

@[expose] public section

noncomputable section

set_option autoImplicit false

universe uR uS

namespace LinearMap

variable {R : Type uR} {S : Type uS}
variable [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]

/-- Scalar extension of an algebra endomorphism to `R / I`, transported from
the tensor-product presentation to the quotient presentation `S / I S`.

This is the arbitrary-linear-map analogue of quotient base change for
algebra norms; it reuses the same canonical tensor/quotient equivalence. -/
noncomputable def quotientBaseChange (f : S →ₗ[R] S) (I : Ideal R) :
    (S ⧸ I.map (algebraMap R S)) →ₗ[R ⧸ I]
      (S ⧸ I.map (algebraMap R S)) := by
  let e := Algebra.TensorProduct.quotIdealMapEquivQuotTensor S I
  exact e.symm.toLinearEquiv.conj (f.baseChange (R ⧸ I))

/-- Quotient base change sends a represented class to the class of its image
under the original endomorphism. -/
@[simp]
theorem quotientBaseChange_mk (f : S →ₗ[R] S) (I : Ideal R) (x : S) :
    f.quotientBaseChange I
        (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.map (algebraMap R S)) x) =
      Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.map (algebraMap R S)) (f x) := by
  let e := Algebra.TensorProduct.quotIdealMapEquivQuotTensor S I
  apply e.injective
  simp [quotientBaseChange, e]

section Finite

variable [Module.Free R S] [Module.Finite R S]

/-- The determinant of quotient base change is the reduction of the original
determinant modulo the base ideal. -/
theorem det_quotientBaseChange (f : S →ₗ[R] S) (I : Ideal R) :
    (f.quotientBaseChange I).det = Ideal.Quotient.mk I f.det := by
  let e := Algebra.TensorProduct.quotIdealMapEquivQuotTensor S I
  change LinearMap.det
      (e.symm.toLinearEquiv.conj (f.baseChange (R ⧸ I))) = _
  calc
    _ = LinearMap.det (f.baseChange (R ⧸ I)) := by
      rw [LinearEquiv.conj_apply, LinearMap.comp_assoc]
      exact LinearMap.det_conj
        (f.baseChange (R ⧸ I)) e.symm.toLinearEquiv
    _ = _ := LinearMap.det_baseChange f

section Local

variable [IsLocalRing R]

/-- If the endomorphism induced on the closed fiber of a finite free algebra
is bijective, then the original determinant is a unit of the local base. -/
theorem isUnit_det_of_bijective_quotientBaseChange
    (f : S →ₗ[R] S)
    (hf : Function.Bijective
      (f.quotientBaseChange (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R))) :
    IsUnit f.det := by
  apply (IsLocalRing.residue_ne_zero_iff_isUnit f.det).mp
  change Ideal.Quotient.mk (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) f.det ≠ 0
  rw [← det_quotientBaseChange]
  exact (LinearEquiv.ofBijective _ hf).isUnit_det'.ne_zero

/-- The determinant unit supplied by bijectivity of the closed-fiber
endomorphism. -/
noncomputable def detUnitOfBijectiveQuotientBaseChange
    (f : S →ₗ[R] S)
    (hf : Function.Bijective
      (f.quotientBaseChange (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R))) : Rˣ :=
  (isUnit_det_of_bijective_quotientBaseChange f hf).unit

/-- The underlying value of the determinant unit is the original
determinant. -/
@[simp]
theorem coe_detUnitOfBijectiveQuotientBaseChange
    (f : S →ₗ[R] S)
    (hf : Function.Bijective
      (f.quotientBaseChange (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R))) :
    (detUnitOfBijectiveQuotientBaseChange f hf : R) = f.det :=
  (isUnit_det_of_bijective_quotientBaseChange f hf).unit_spec

/-- The residue of the bundled determinant unit is the determinant unit of
the induced closed-fiber equivalence. -/
theorem residue_detUnitOfBijectiveQuotientBaseChange
    (f : S →ₗ[R] S)
    (hf : Function.Bijective
      (f.quotientBaseChange (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R))) :
    Units.map
        (Ideal.Quotient.mk (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)).toMonoidHom
        (detUnitOfBijectiveQuotientBaseChange f hf) =
      LinearEquiv.det
        (LinearEquiv.ofBijective
          (f.quotientBaseChange (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)) hf) := by
  apply Units.ext
  simp only [Units.coe_map, LinearEquiv.coe_det,
    coe_detUnitOfBijectiveQuotientBaseChange]
  change Ideal.Quotient.mk (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) f.det =
    (f.quotientBaseChange (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)).det
  rw [det_quotientBaseChange]

end Local

end Finite

end LinearMap

end
